2.2.13-003.comment: You need to set the disc to the next half-hour mark after you arrive. So if you arrive at 10:40 AM, set it to 11:00 AM. The duration of parking doesn't matter.

2.2.13-004.question_text: You're going to park in a spot with a parking meter. What do you need to keep in mind?

options.text: Display a valid parking ticket clearly visible from outside
Don't exceed the parking time on the ticket
A parking ticket is always unnecessary if you use a parking disc

2.2.13-004.comment: You need to place the valid parking ticket where it's clearly visible from outside the vehicle. Make sure not to exceed the parking time printed on the ticket. A parking disc can only replace a parking ticket if the parking meter or machine is broken.

2.2.13-101.question_text: What is allowed when stopping at non-working parking meters?

options.text: To let passengers in or out
To load or unload
For a quick shopping trip

2.2.13-101.comment: You don't need to monitor the parking time when letting passengers in or out, or when loading or unloading.

2.2.14-102.question_text: What should you do when leaving your car?

options.text: Check for oncoming traffic before opening the door
Secure the vehicle against rolling away
Secure the vehicle against unauthorized use

2.2.14-102.comment: Before leaving your vehicle, make sure it's secured against rolling away, especially on a slope. Check for other road users before getting out, and make sure your passengers do the same. Opening doors carelessly can lead to accidents.

2.2.14-104.question_text: Your car is parked at the roadside. What's the right way to get in?

options.text: Let passengers get in from the sidewalk if possible
Only open doors on the road side when traffic allows
Opening doors on the right side is always safe

2.2.14-104.comment: When getting in or out, you need to make sure you don't endanger other road users. Getting in from the right side, from the sidewalk, is safer, but not always risk-free. Before opening the doors, check that traffic allows it, and ensure there are no pedestrians or cyclists on the sidewalk.

2.2.14-107-M.question_text: Why can't you get out now?

options.text: Because of the cyclist
Because of the motorcycle
Because of the pedestrian

2.2.14-107-M.comment: When getting in or out, you need to make sure you don't put other road users at risk. There's a cyclist coming up in your left mirror, so you need to let them pass first.

2.2.14-108-M.question_text: You've stopped in a parking lane and want to get out. How should you act in this situation?

options.text: - check the left mirror before opening the door
- look over your shoulder to the left before opening the door
- only through the slightly opened door

2.2.14-108-M.comment: Before you open the door and get out, you need to check your left mirror to make sure no one is coming from behind. Also, do a shoulder check to the left to ensure there are no other road users in your blind spot.

2.2.14-109.question_text: How do you secure your car against unauthorized use when leaving it?

options.text: I lock the doors
I close the windows
I activate the child safety locks

2.2.14-109.comment: You need to make sure that unauthorized people can't use your vehicle. So, take out the ignition key and make sure all windows and doors are closed.

2.2.15-105.question_text: A car with power steering has broken down due to engine failure and needs to be towed. What's correct?

options.text: - it's much harder to steer
- it's blocked
- it's not affected

2.2.15-105.comment: The power steering only works when the engine is running. If the engine fails, steering becomes significantly harder, and you'll need more strength. The steering is affected.

2.2.15-107.question_text: How should you secure a vehicle that has broken down at a spot where it poses a danger to other traffic at night?

options.text: Turn on the hazard lights immediately
Set up a warning triangle at a safe distance
Turn on the reverse lights

2.2.15-107.comment: If a vehicle breaks down on a multi-lane road where it can't be seen in time as a stationary obstacle, you must turn on the hazard lights immediately. Then, place a warning triangle visibly at a safe distance, about 100 meters ahead of the vehicle in fast traffic. You don't need to turn on the reverse lights.

2.2.15-109.question_text: What should you keep in mind when towing?

options.text: The distance between the vehicles must not be more than 5 meters
The tow rope/tow bar must be clearly marked
Motorcycles can only be towed with a solid connection

2.2.15-109.comment: When towing, the distance between the towing vehicle and the towed vehicle must not exceed 5 meters. The tools used, like a bar or rope, must be clearly marked. Motorcycles can't be towed; they must be loaded instead.

2.2.15-110.question_text: Your car has a flat tire on the highway. How should you behave?

options.text: - turn on the hazard lights and pull over as far to the right as possible
- set up the warning triangle about 100 meters away
- keep driving to the next exit

2.2.15-110.comment: If your vehicle breaks down on a multi-lane road due to a flat tire and can't be seen in time as a stationary obstacle, turn on the hazard lights immediately. Then, place a warning triangle visibly at a safe distance, about 100 meters from the vehicle in fast traffic.

2.2.15-111.question_text: Your car has a defect and is no longer drivable. What should you keep in mind when towing?

options.text: - both vehicles must turn on hazard lights
- the tow rope should be kept as taut as possible
- the highway may only be used as a shortcut to the next workshop

2.2.15-111.comment: When towing, both the towing vehicle and the towed vehicle must have their hazard lights on. The tow rope should be kept as taut as possible. If the breakdown didn't happen on the highway, you can't enter the highway while towing.

2.2.15-112.question_text: Your car has a defect and is no longer drivable. What should you keep in mind when towing?

options.text: - both vehicles must turn on hazard lights
- the tow rope should be kept as taut as possible
- the highway may only be used as a shortcut to the next workshop

2.2.15-112.comment: When towing, both the towing vehicle and the towed vehicle must have their hazard lights on. The tow rope should be kept as taut as possible. If the breakdown didn't happen on the highway, you can't enter the highway while towing.

2.2.15-114.question_text: Your car has a engine failure and needs to be towed with a tow rope. What do you need to keep in mind?

options.text: A car with power steering is harder to steer when broken
When towing an electric vehicle, you must follow the manufacturer's guidelines
You need at least the driver's license class BE for towing a car

2.2.15-114.comment: Make sure to follow the manufacturer's guidelines when towing. The electronic aids won't work, so be prepared for a heavy steering.

2.2.15-115.question_text: You have a breakdown outside of town. Your vehicle is behind a curve on the road. What is correct in this situation?

options.text: I must turn on the hazard lights
I must place a clearly visible warning sign at least 100 m behind the vehicle
I should wear a safety vest

2.2.15-115.comment: Before leaving your vehicle, you need to turn on the hazard lights and put on a safety vest. This way, other road users can see you and react. Outside of town, you must place a warning triangle 100 m away from the vehicle.

2.2.16-001.question_text: Where can you use the high beam to indicate your intention to overtake?

options.text: Outside of town during the day
Outside of town at night
In town at night

2.2.16-001.comment: As a driver, you can use the high beam outside of built-up areas to signal your intention to overtake. This is allowed both during the day and at night. In built-up areas, you can't use the high beam.

2.2.16-101.question_text: When do you need to turn on the hazard lights in your vehicle?

options.text: If there's a breakdown in a difficult spot
When being towed
If I park briefly in the second row

2.2.16-101.comment: If you have a breakdown in a difficult spot, you should warn other road users with your hazard lights. You also need to turn on the hazard lights when your car is being towed.

2.2.17-001.question_text: How can you tell if the fog lights are on?

options.text: By the yellow warning light
By the blue warning light
By the red warning light

2.2.17-001.comment: A quick look at the dashboard is enough, and the driver can immediately see from the yellow warning light that the fog lights are on. According to the regulations, the warning light must be in the driver's direct line of sight.

2.2.17-005.question_text: Visibility is significantly impaired. When can you turn on the fog lights?

options.text: In rain
In snowfall
In fog

2.2.17-005.comment: If visibility is severely impaired during the day due to fog, snowfall, or rain, you must turn on your dipped headlights. You can also turn on the fog lights only in such weather conditions with strong visibility impairment.

2.2.17-008.question_text: You're driving at night on an unlit road. A vehicle is driving closely ahead. What lights must you have on?

options.text: Dipped headlights
High beam
Parking lights only

2.2.17-008.comment: The driver must turn on the dipped headlights to avoid blinding the vehicle ahead or oncoming traffic. Using the high beam isn't an option since it would blind the other driver.

2.2.17-010.question_text: The rear lights of your vehicle are covered. What should you do?

options.text: Must be installed in any case
Only to be installed during twilight or darkness
Only to be installed for distances over 5 km

2.2.17-010.comment: You must install a light carrier with all rear lighting devices on your vehicle in any case. Remember, as a driver, you're responsible for the effectiveness of the lighting. There's no distance limit in this situation.

2.2.17-012.question_text: Which lighting device must you turn on when driving in the dark?

options.text: Dipped headlights
Only parking lights
High beam

2.2.17-012.comment: In Germany, it's required to turn on the dipped headlights when it's dark. With the dipped headlights on, you see better and are also seen better.

2.2.17-101.question_text: When can you turn on fog lights during the day?

options.text: - Fog or snowfall
- Rain
- Ice on the windshield

2.2.17-101.comment: You can use fog lights during the day when visibility is severely reduced due to fog, snowfall, or rain. These conditions usually happen in the fall and winter months. You shouldn't drive with ice on your windshield; it needs to be cleared before you drive.

2.2.17-102.question_text: When can you turn on rear fog lights?

options.text: When visibility is less than 50 m due to fog
When visibility is 100 m due to fog
When visibility is reduced due to heavy rain

2.2.17-102.comment: You can only use your rear fog lights when visibility is below 50 m due to heavy fog. If you use them in other conditions, they can blind other drivers and create a safety risk.

2.2.17-103.question_text: Where is it enough to use parking lights when parking a car on unlit roads?

options.text: Within built-up areas
Outside built-up areas
On the shoulders of highways

2.2.17-103.comment: You can only park with parking lights on unlit roads within built-up areas. This is because cars drive slower there, making it easier for others to see parked vehicles. It's not allowed outside built-up areas.

2.2.17-109.question_text: When must you use dipped headlights during the day?

options.text: - Fog or snowfall
- Rain
- Fogged-up windshield

2.2.17-109.comment: You must use your dipped headlights during the day when visibility is severely limited due to rain, fog, or snowfall. This helps you be seen better by other road users and allows you to see them better too.

2.2.17-111.question_text: In which cases do you only need to turn on the position lights (parking lights) at dusk or darkness?

options.text: When parked on the shoulder outside built-up areas
When driving on well-lit roads

2.2.17-111.comment: Always drive with dipped headlights at dusk and darkness. This way, you can see well and be seen well. You should never drive only with position lights, as they aren't bright enough for that.

2.2.17-114.question_text: When must you turn on dipped headlights?

options.text: During dusk
In darkness
When driving through a tunnel

2.2.17-114.comment: To ensure you're seen, use your dipped headlights during dusk, in darkness, and when driving through a tunnel.

2.2.17-115.question_text: What can a wrong setting of the manual headlight adjustment lead to?

options.text: Oncoming traffic can be blinded by my dipped headlights
The light range in front of my vehicle can be too low
The lifespan of the dipped headlight bulb can be reduced

2.2.17-115.comment: If your headlights are set too high, you can blind oncoming traffic. If they're set too low, they won't illuminate the road properly, and you won't have enough visibility ahead. Incorrectly adjusted headlights can also lead to them not functioning properly.

2.2.17-402.question_text: You're driving at night with high beams. When must you switch to low beams?

options.text: When a vehicle is coming towards you
When a vehicle is driving ahead of you at a close distance
When people are walking ahead in the same direction

2.2.17-402.comment: You must not blind oncoming traffic with your high beams. So, turn them off as soon as you see other vehicles coming towards you. Pedestrians walking in the same direction as you won't be blinded by your high beams.

2.2.17-403.question_text: You're driving at night with high beams. When must you switch to low beams?

options.text: When I'm on a road with continuous, sufficient lighting
When I have to wait at a level crossing and might blind others
When pedestrians are walking ahead in the same direction

2.2.17-403.comment: When driving at night with high beams, you need to switch to low beams when you see oncoming traffic. You shouldn't use high beams on well-lit roads. Waiting vehicles shouldn't blind anyone, so turn off your high beams at level crossings. Pedestrians walking in the same direction won't be blinded by your high beams.

2.2.17-404.question_text: Why must you also drive with dipped headlights during the day if visibility is significantly reduced due to fog, rain, or snowfall?

options.text: To be seen better by other road users
To drive at higher speeds
To see traffic signs from a greater distance

2.2.17-404.comment: In poor visibility conditions during the day, caused by rain, fog, or snow, you must turn on your dipped headlights. The main goal is for your vehicle to be seen better by others. It doesn't help you see traffic signs from a greater distance.

2.2.18-003.question_text: What is the recommended speed for cars and motorcycles on highways?
2.2.18-003.comment: On highways, cars and motorcycles should stick to a recommended speed of 130 km/h. Also, only vehicles that can go faster than 60 km/h are allowed on the highway.

2.2.18-006.question_text: You're approaching a vehicle on the left lane that is just starting to overtake. What do you do?

options.text: Keep a safe distance from the vehicle ahead
Let the vehicle ahead overtake
Tailgate, honk, and signal

2.2.18-006.comment: You should allow the vehicle to overtake by keeping a safe distance. Since the vehicle is changing lanes from the right, be prepared for it to be slower than you, even if it speeds up. Slow down if needed. Never tailgate, honk, or signal in this situation.

2.2.18-007.question_text: You're driving on a highway with light traffic. How long can you use the left lane?

options.text: As long as needed to overtake other vehicles
As long as you're following a vehicle that's overtaking in the left lane
Constantly, as long as no other vehicle wants to overtake you

2.2.18-007.comment: The left lane is only for overtaking because in Germany, you must drive on the right. If the vehicle ahead is overtaking in the left lane, it's likely that other drivers will want to overtake too. So, it's okay to use the left lane in this case.

options.text: U-turns are prohibited
Entry only at intersections and junctions
You can drive faster at night than the range of your low beams allows

2.2.18-009.comment: You can only enter expressways at intersections or junctions. U-turns are not allowed. The speed rules are different from those on highways. You must not drive faster than the range of your low beams allows on expressways.

2.2.18-011.question_text: There's a traffic jam on a highway with three lanes. Where should you create a lane for emergency vehicles?

options.text: Between the left and middle lanes
Between the middle and right lanes
On the shoulder

2.2.18-011.comment: When traffic is stuck on highways or roads outside built-up areas with at least two lanes in one direction, you need to create a clear lane in the middle of the roadway for police and emergency vehicles. For three-lane roads, this means between the left and middle lanes.

options.text: - far to the right
- far to the left
- in the middle

2.2.18-013.comment: You're approaching the end of a traffic jam on the highway. Turn on your hazard lights. Create a lane in the middle of the roadway for police and emergency vehicles: on three-lane roads, this means between the left and middle lanes. So, you need to move far to the right. This rule applies outside built-up areas and on highways.

options.text: I keep driving
I merge onto the shoulder
I stay in my lane and wait for a gap

2.2.18-014.comment: You want to exit the highway. You see that traffic is jammed at your intended exit. Since you can't drive on the shoulder and can't stop in your lane, the correct action is to keep driving and use the next exit to leave the highway.

2.2.18-015-M.question_text: How should you behave if a traffic jam forms on this road?

options.text: - as far left as possible
- as far right as possible
- still in the middle

2.2.18-015-M.comment: Every driver must help create a clear lane in the middle of the roadway for police and emergency vehicles when a traffic jam forms on highways and roads outside built-up areas with more than one lane. Don't drive on the shoulder, as that's prohibited.

2.2.18-016-M.question_text: How do you behave correctly now?

options.text: I warn the driver with sound and light signals
I drive as far right as possible
I notify the police

2.2.18-016-M.comment: Watch out for wrong-way drivers! You should warn the driver with sound (horn) and light signals, and notify the police. Also, please drive as far right as possible.

options.text: I speed up and merge in front of the truck
I slow down and merge between the red car and the truck
I slow down and merge after the yellow vehicle

2.2.18-017-M.comment: You've already passed the truck that's driving in the right lane of the highway. If you speed up now, you can merge onto the main road before the end of the lane. That's what you should do.

2.2.18-018-M.question_text: You want to leave the highway. How should you act in this situation?

options.text: I switch to the left lane
I watch out for oncoming vehicles
I continue on the shoulder

2.2.18-018-M.comment: Both the illuminated arrow and the sign indicate a lane change. Please switch to the left lane.

2.2.18-019.question_text: How should you behave in a traffic jam on highways and on main roads with two lanes in one direction?

options.text: - drive as far right as possible in the right lane
- drive as far left as possible in the left lane
- drive as far left as possible in the right lane

2.2.18-019.comment: You should either drive as far left as possible in the left lane or as far right as possible in the right lane to create a rescue lane.

2.2.18-021-M.question_text: How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: I stay in the middle lane
I switch to the left lane
I switch to the right lane

2.2.18-021-M.comment: You need to stay in the middle lane because there are vehicles in the left and right lanes that you would obstruct. A motorcycle is coming from the on-ramp onto the highway in the right lane, and a car that just passed you is in the left lane.

2.2.18-101.question_text: Your vehicle has broken down on the highway. What should you keep in mind when being towed?

options.text: The highway must be exited at the next exit
Both vehicles must turn on their hazard lights while towing
The highway may be driven on until the exit closest to a suitable workshop

2.2.18-101.comment: When towing on the highway, both the towing vehicle and the towed vehicle must have their hazard lights on. Towing is only allowed on the highway until the next exit, where you must leave the highway.

2.2.18-103.question_text: You're driving on the highway and missed your exit. How should you behave correctly?

options.text: I keep driving and leave the highway at one of the next exits
I drive back on the shoulder if the exit is less than 100 m away
I stop on the shoulder to plan my further route

2.2.18-103.comment: Keep driving until the next exit and leave the highway there. You can then return to the missed exit from the other side of the highway. You must not stop or drive in reverse.

2.2.18-104-M.question_text: How can a lane change assistant without steering intervention support you in this situation?

options.text: - warns of a collision with a vehicle in the middle lane
- independently performs a lane change
- slows my vehicle down

2.2.18-104-M.comment: The lane change assistant detects the vehicle in the middle lane as a danger and warns you not to switch to that lane. It would require steering intervention to perform a lane change independently. The lane change assistant does not interfere with your speed.

2.2.18-215.question_text: Why should traffic radio be turned on during highway driving?

options.text: - warns of wrong-way drivers
- informs about traffic jams
- is required during highway driving

2.2.18-215.comment: Traffic radio warns of wrong-way drivers and informs about traffic jams. It's not required, though.

2.2.21-007.question_text: Why is it dangerous if people in the back seats don't wear seat belts?

options.text: - injuries can occur even at low speeds
- it can endanger the people in the front seats
- these people can be thrown out of the vehicle

2.2.21-007.comment: In a collision, people in the back seats can be thrown forward or sideways. If they are thrown forward, the front seat backs don't provide enough protection. As a result, the driver and front passenger are also at risk. Injuries can happen even at low speeds.

2.2.21-105.question_text: How can you safely transport a five-year-old child in your car?

options.text: In an appropriate child seat with a safety mark
On a back seat with a standard three-point seat belt
On the back bench with a fastened lap belt

2.2.21-105.comment: If you want to take a five-year-old child in your car, you must use a tested child seat that fits the child's size. This is required for all children under 12.

2.2.21-111.question_text: At what collision speed should you expect serious or fatal injuries if you're not wearing a seat belt?

options.text: From 30 km/h
From 50 km/h
From 80 km/h

2.2.21-111.comment: Without a seat belt, serious injuries can occur even in a collision just above 20 km/h. This applies to rear-end collisions, which are often mistakenly considered harmless. Always buckle up, even for short distances.

2.2.21-112.question_text: A car is equipped with two front airbags. Where must seat belts be worn?

options.text: On all seats
Not on the front seats
Only on the front seats

2.2.21-112.comment: The front airbags protect the driver and front passenger during a strong impact, like a rear-end collision. However, they don't provide complete protection. All passengers must wear seat belts on every trip.

2.2.21-114.question_text: You want to take several small children home after a birthday party. What should you consider when transporting them in your car?

options.text: The children must be secured with the required restraint systems
Restraint systems for children don't need to be used in built-up areas
Just buckling the children with the available seat belts is enough

2.2.21-114.comment: If you're taking several small children home in your car, you need to make sure that all your passengers are secured with the legally required restraint systems.

2.2.21-118.question_text: While driving, the airbag warning light is constantly on. What should you do?

options.text: Visit a workshop
Remove the vehicle from traffic immediately
Do nothing, as it's a signal for the workshop

2.2.21-118.comment: The airbag warning light indicates a problem with the airbag system. Usually, only a workshop can fix this issue. You don't need to take the vehicle off the road immediately.

2.2.21-121.question_text: How can you prevent a child from opening a rear door while driving?

options.text: Use the child safety locks on the rear doors
Use the central locking system

2.2.21-121.comment: Child safety locks let you lock the rear doors separately. This stops a child from opening the door while you're driving, keeping them safe.

2.2.21-122.question_text: You want to take a child in your car. When do you need to use a child seat?

options.text: If the child is younger than 12 years and shorter than 150 cm
If the child is older than 12 years and taller than 150 cm
If the child is older than 12 years and shorter than 150 cm

2.2.21-122.comment: You need a child seat if the child is younger than 12 years and shorter than 150 cm. If you don't have one, you risk getting a fine.

2.2.21-123.question_text: You want to take a baby in a car seat on the passenger seat. What do you need to consider when using a baby carrier?

options.text: The baby carrier must be installed facing the rear
The passenger airbag must be deactivated
The baby must be strapped in the baby carrier

2.2.21-123.comment: The baby carrier should be installed facing the rear, and the passenger airbag needs to be turned off to protect the baby. Babies don't have strong muscles to handle impacts.

2.2.22-104.question_text: What should you do when transporting bicycles on the roof of your car?

options.text: Secure the bikes and the holding device
Avoid high speeds
Check the fastening regularly

2.2.22-104.comment: Transporting bikes on the roof requires extra attention: make sure everything is securely fastened and check the attachments during breaks. High speeds can worsen handling.

2.2.22-105.question_text: What should you check when transporting bicycles on a rear rack?

options.text: If the system is suitable for the vehicle according to the manufacturer's instructions
If the system and bicycles are securely fastened
If lights or the license plate are covered

2.2.22-105.comment: Make sure the rear rack is securely attached and that the bicycles are fastened properly. If lights or the license plate are covered, you need to add proper lighting or a license plate holder.

2.2.22-108.question_text: How should you mark a load that extends more than 40 cm beyond the vehicle's side lights at night or in poor visibility?

options.text: With white light in front
With red light in the back
By turning on the hazard lights

2.2.22-108.comment: At night or in bad visibility, a load extending more than 40 cm beyond the vehicle's side lights must be marked with additional lights. A white light in front and a red light in the back are required.

2.2.22-109.question_text: How high can a red light marking a load extending to the rear be mounted above the road?
2.2.22-109.comment: The maximum height for the light is 1.5 meters. This ensures it's visible to other road users. If it's higher, it might be overlooked.

2.2.22-111.question_text: How far can a load extend forward from the vehicle?
2.2.22-111.comment: A load can only extend forward if it's at least 2.5 meters high from the front edge of the vehicle. It can then only extend 0.5 meters forward. These limits are for safety reasons.

2.2.22-117.question_text: What should you consider when loading vehicles?

options.text: Load that extends more than 1 m beyond the rear reflectors must be marked
Load above a height of 2.50 m may extend a maximum of 50 cm forward
Heavy loads do not need to be secured

2.2.22-117.comment: When loading your vehicle, make sure that any load extending more than 1 m beyond the rear reflectors is marked and that any load above 2.50 m in height only extends a maximum of 50 cm forward.

2.2.22-122.question_text: What do you need to consider when you want to transport a load?

options.text: - must be secured
- must not cause avoidable noise
- may extend sideways as individual rods

2.2.22-122.comment: When loading your vehicle, you need to ensure that the load is securely fastened. Items that are hard to see, as well as poles, rods, or boards, shouldn't extend out of the vehicle's interior. The load should be stowed in a way that doesn't cause any avoidable noise.

2.2.22-123.question_text: You want to carry vacation luggage on the roof of your fully occupied car. What do you need to consider?

options.text: The manufacturer's specification for roof load in the owner's manual
The permissible total weight of my car
The roof load specification in the registration certificate part I

2.2.22-123.comment: Pay attention to the permissible roof load specified by the manufacturer, which you can find in the owner's manual. The roof load isn't noted in the registration certificate part I. You also shouldn't exceed the vehicle's total permissible weight. Unevenly distributed loads can affect stability when braking and turning.

2.2.22-124.question_text: You want to transport a load. What do you need to consider?

options.text: I must not be obstructed by the load while driving
The vehicle's traffic safety must not be compromised
The load must not shift or fall over during the drive

2.2.22-124.comment: When transporting a load, you need to ensure that you're not obstructed by it while driving, that the vehicle's traffic safety isn't compromised, and that the load doesn't shift or fall over during the trip.

2.2.22-125.question_text: What are load securing devices for use in a car?

options.text: Tie-down straps
Safety nets
Wheel chocks

2.2.22-125.comment: Load securing devices for use in a car include tie-down straps and safety nets. Wheel chocks are not included.

2.2.22-126.question_text: You want to transport a load on the roof of your car. How does this affect your car's handling?

options.text: The braking distance increases
Acceleration ability decreases
Sensitivity to crosswinds decreases

2.2.22-126.comment: Carrying a load on the roof will affect your handling by increasing the braking distance and decreasing your acceleration ability (like when overtaking).

2.2.22-127.question_text: What is a way to secure a load in a car?

options.text: The luggage net
The tension strap
The anti-slip mat

2.2.22-127.comment: The anti-slip mat prevents the load from sliding. Tension straps are used to secure the load down. The luggage net keeps the load from flying around.

2.2.22-128.question_text: What should you consider when loading a trunk with luggage?

options.text: - store the warning triangle in an easily accessible place
- store heavy luggage at the bottom
- secure the luggage against shifting

2.2.22-128.comment: In case of an accident or breakdown, the warning triangle should always be easily accessible so you can set it up quickly. The load should be secured against shifting to prevent it from flying around during hard acceleration, braking, or turning. Heavy luggage should be stored at the bottom to avoid it falling.

2.2.22-129.question_text: How far can a marked load extend beyond your vehicle at the back if your journey is more than 100 km?
2.2.22-129.comment: For journeys up to 100 kilometers, the load can extend up to 3 meters at the back. For journeys over 100 kilometers, it can extend up to 1.5 meters.

2.2.23-034.question_text: What’s important about official license plates?

options.text: They must be securely attached in the designated spots
They must always be clearly readable
The rear plates must be illuminated at night

2.2.23-034.comment: For official license plates, it’s important that they are attached in the required place. They also need to be clearly readable and illuminated at night.

2.2.23-035.question_text: What’s required if your vehicle's liability insurance has expired?

options.text: - must not be used in traffic
- must be deregistered at the registration office
- must be presented at the registration office

2.2.23-035.comment: Without valid liability insurance, a vehicle isn’t roadworthy and can’t be used in public traffic. Liability insurance covers damages you might cause to other vehicles and people. If you don’t have it, you must deregister the vehicle at the registration office, or you could face penalties.

2.2.23-036.question_text: What can you change on an official license plate?

options.text: Nothing can be changed
Put a film on it to protect the lettering
Add colorful stickers

2.2.23-036.comment: An official license plate is a legal document that must not be altered in any way. So, don’t put films or stickers on your license plate.

2.2.23-053.question_text: Which change must you report to the relevant registration authority immediately as a vehicle owner?

options.text: - my address
- my name
- my liability insurance

2.2.23-053.comment: If you change your name or address, you need to inform the registration authority. However, you don’t have to report changes to your liability insurance.

2.2.23-054.question_text: You are the new owner of a registered vehicle. What do you need to do?

options.text: - inform the registration authority about the change of ownership
- provide proof of liability insurance for the vehicle to the registration authority
- generally have a main inspection done when changing ownership

2.2.23-054.comment: When changing ownership, you don’t need to have a main inspection done since it remains valid. You need to inform the registration authority about the ownership change and provide proof of liability insurance so they can register the vehicle under the new owner.

2.2.23-101.question_text: What should you consider with vehicles that have tarpaulins?

options.text: The tarpaulins must not obstruct the driver's view through the mirrors
Unloaded trailers with high tarpaulin structures are particularly sensitive to side winds
For vehicles with tarpaulins, special securing of the load can be omitted

2.2.23-101.comment: With vehicles that have tarpaulins, you need to ensure that the view to the rear isn’t blocked. Unloaded trailers with tall tarpaulin structures can be at risk from side winds.

2.2.23-104.question_text: How do you secure a car with a manual transmission on a hill to prevent rolling?

options.text: Engage the parking brake
Put it in first gear or reverse
Put the gear lever in neutral

2.2.23-104.comment: To secure a car with a manual transmission against rolling, you should put it in a low gear like first gear or reverse. Engage the parking brake and don’t put the gear lever in neutral.

options.text: The load
Worn wiper blades (causing streaks)
Dirty windows

2.2.23-107.comment: Your visibility can be affected if the windows are dirty, if worn wipers create streaks, or if the load blocks your view.

2.2.23-113.question_text: How do you secure a single-axle trailer with surge brakes against rolling when parked on a slope?

options.text: Engage the parking brake
Place wheel chocks in front of the wheels
Place one wheel chock in front and one behind a wheel

2.2.23-113.comment: To prevent your trailer from rolling away, you need to place wheel chocks in front of the wheels and also secure the trailer with the parking brake.

2.2.23-119.question_text: What should you consider when adjusting headrests in the vehicle?

options.text: The highest part of your head should be about level with the top of the headrest
The distance between the back of your head and the headrest should be as small as possible
The top of the headrest should align with the upper neck vertebra

2.2.23-119.comment: Properly adjusted headrests reduce the impact on your neck during sudden vehicle movements. They protect passengers in case of accidents. You should adjust the headrest so that the top of your head is level with the top of the headrest. To maximize its protective function, the headrest should be tilted so that the back of your head is only a few centimeters away from it.

2.2.23-120.question_text: When should you refrain from making phone calls even with a hands-free device?

options.text: During difficult conversations
In complicated traffic situations
If it distracts me

2.2.23-120.comment: Even with a hands-free device, having a difficult conversation can be dangerous while driving. It can distract you. Avoid making calls in complicated traffic situations.

2.2.23-121.question_text: You want to use your smartphone mounted in the vehicle as a navigation device. What should you keep in mind?

options.text: Enter the destination while the vehicle is stationary
Try not to operate the device while driving
Use the device's voice output

2.2.23-121.comment: To stay safe, you should enter your destination while the vehicle is stationary and try not to operate the device while driving. Using the voice output helps you stay focused on the traffic.

2.2.23-122.question_text: During your drive, you receive a call. What should you keep in mind?

options.text: The phone should not be held for this
Using the phone should only require a quick glance
The phone should not be used for more than 7 seconds

2.2.23-122.comment: Using your phone is prohibited if it distracts you too much from the traffic. This inevitably happens when you pick it up and look at the display.

2.2.23-124.question_text: What’s the main function of the headrest in a car?

options.text: - increases safety for passengers
- improves seating position
- replaces the seatbelt in the back seat

2.2.23-124.comment: The headrest helps reduce the impact on passengers' necks during hard braking or accidents.

2.2.26-102.question_text: You unexpectedly stop at a pedestrian crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Move a bit forward or backward to clear the crossing as much as possible
Partially drive onto the sidewalk to clear the crossing
Never drive backward, even if it's clear behind you

2.2.26-102.comment: To avoid danger for pedestrians, you need to keep pedestrian crossings clear. So, you should move out of the way as quickly as possible. Drive carefully forward or backward, as traffic allows, but don’t drive onto the sidewalk since it’s only for pedestrians.

2.2.29-001.question_text: What can participating in illegal street races lead to?

options.text: The occurrence of serious traffic accidents
A prison sentence for the driver
The revocation of the driver's license for the driver

2.2.29-001.comment: Taking part in illegal street races can result in serious traffic accidents, a prison sentence for the driver, and possibly losing their driver's license.

2.2.30-103.question_text: Which motor vehicles are banned from driving on Sundays and holidays when transporting goods for profit?

options.text: For trucks with a permissible total weight over 7.5 tons
For trucks with a trailer
For cars with a trailer

2.2.30-103.comment: The driving ban on Sundays and holidays applies to Class C vehicles, meaning trucks with trailers or trucks over 7.5 tons. Cars can still drive.

2.2.32-101.question_text: You drive onto a public road from an unpaved area (like a field or construction site) and make it very dirty. Who's responsible for cleaning this traffic obstruction?

options.text: You as the cause
The responsible road construction office
The residents of that road section

2.2.32-101.comment: If you dirty a road by driving out from an unpaved area, you have to clean it up since you caused it.

2.2.32-102.question_text: What should you do to prevent danger to others from equipment or cargo parts that fell from your vehicle?

options.text: - remove the parts yourself
- secure the danger area and immediately notify road service or police
- keep driving and inform the next regulatory office

2.2.32-102.comment: You need to remove any items that fell onto the road and could endanger other road users. Secure the danger area and notify the police or road service if necessary.

2.2.34-001-M.question_text: How should you behave in this situation?

options.text: I keep driving as I am
I brake hard immediately
I take a photo of the accident scene

2.2.34-001-M.comment: The accident scene is already secured, and the police and ambulance are on site. You can keep driving as you are.

options.text: I reduce my speed further
I drive as far left as possible
I keep driving as I am

2.2.34-003-M.comment: In the event of an accident, you should always play it safe by increasing your following distance and reducing your speed in case someone runs onto the road.

2.2.34-101.question_text: You had a wildlife accident. How should you behave now?

options.text: I secure the accident scene
I notify the police
I take the wildlife with me

2.2.34-101.comment: After a wildlife accident, you should turn on your hazard lights, put on a safety vest, and set up a warning triangle to secure the accident scene. You should notify the police, explain the accident, and give your exact location.

2.2.34-102.question_text: Why should you always carry the European Accident Report while driving?

options.text: - makes it easier to document accidents with foreign-speaking participants
- allows for independent accident documentation by the participants
- clearly answers liability questions at the accident scene

2.2.34-102.comment: You should always carry the European Accident Report because it makes it easier to document accidents with foreign-speaking participants and allows for independent accident documentation.

2.2.37-002.question_text: You're driving at about 40 km/h. About 10 meters ahead, the traffic light changes from green to yellow. What do you do?

options.text: Keep going
Stop

2.2.37-002.comment: At 40 km/h, your braking distance is about 28 meters. Even with an emergency stop, you can't come to a complete stop in time from 10 meters away. To avoid a possible rear-end collision, you should keep going.

2.2.37-003.question_text: You're driving at about 40 km/h. About 40 meters ahead, the traffic light changes from green to yellow. What do you do?

options.text: Stop
Keep going

2.2.37-003.comment: According to the rule of thumb, your car will stop after 28 meters at 40 km/h. So the only correct reaction is to stop.

2.2.37-007.question_text: What applies to permanent traffic signals?

options.text: Permanent signals block or allow the lane
There's a no stopping rule on lanes with permanent signals
Permanent signals only apply to multi-lane vehicles

2.2.37-007.comment: Permanent signals (placed above the lane) either block the lane or allow it to be used, and there is a no stopping rule on lanes with permanent signals.

2.2.37-008.question_text: What do these permanent signals mean?

options.text: - 1 can continue driving
- 2 must switch to the right lane
- 3 and 4 must stop

2.2.37-008.comment: The permanent signal on lane 1 (green) means you can keep going. Number 2 (yellow) must switch to the right lane to continue on lane 1. 3 and 4 are incorrect (red).

2.2.38-101.question_text: A vehicle with flashing blue lights and siren is approaching from behind. What should you do?

options.text: Drive as far to the right as possible
Slow down
Stop immediately

2.2.38-101.comment: You need to give the vehicle a clear path. So, you should slow down and move as far to the side of the road as you can, allowing the vehicle with blue lights to pass without obstruction.

2.4.40-002.question_text: How should you behave on a highway with this traffic sign?

options.text: Increase attention, increase distance
Slow down and turn on hazard lights in a traffic jam
Switch to the shoulder and keep driving in a traffic jam

2.4.40-002.comment: Warning of a traffic jam: With this sign, you should reduce your speed and increase the distance to the vehicle in front. Get a better view of the situation by watching the traffic ahead and, if necessary, drive slightly offset within your lane. Turn on your hazard lights when approaching the end of a traffic jam.

2.4.40-003.question_text: How should you behave with this traffic sign?

options.text: Reduce speed before the curve
Drive as far to the right as possible
Signal left before the curve

2.4.40-003.comment: This traffic sign warns of a dangerous left curve. Slow down to minimize centrifugal force. Oncoming traffic could drift into your lane due to centrifugal force, and a vehicle might be stalled just around the curve. So, drive as far to the right as possible. You're following the road, not turning, so you don't need to signal.

2.4.40-004.question_text: How should you behave in this danger zone?

options.text: Drive slower, watch for wildlife
Dim your lights and brake if you see wildlife
Don't swerve for wildlife if it endangers oncoming traffic

2.4.40-004.comment: Warning of wildlife crossing: This sign is placed in areas where wildlife accidents have occurred. As soon as you see this sign, you should reduce your speed and be ready to brake. Pay special attention to the roadside. If you see wildlife, brake and dim your lights. If wildlife suddenly jumps in front of you, perform an emergency stop. Avoid swerving, as that could lead you into oncoming traffic.

2.4.40-007.question_text: What should you expect with this traffic sign?

options.text: Vehicles in front suddenly swerving left
Vehicles in front suddenly braking
Branches lying on the road

2.4.40-007.comment: Due to trees, tall vehicles might suddenly brake or swerve. When passing by, tall vehicles can break off branches, which then end up on the road. So, be especially attentive.

2.4.41-004-M.question_text: You're driving on this highway. How should you behave?

options.text: I switch to the right lane
I only use the left lane in case of a breakdown
I stay in my current lane

2.4.41-004-M.comment: On highways, the rule is to drive on the right. So, you need to be in the right lane unless you're overtaking. There's no one in front of you to overtake. The left lane is closed, and you can't use it, even if you have a breakdown.

2.4.41-101.question_text: What do you need to pay attention to with this traffic sign?

options.text: Use snow chains
Maximum speed 50 km/h
Vehicles with chains have right of way

2.4.41-101.comment: This sign indicates that the following road can only be used with snow chains. It's forbidden to enter without them. The maximum speed with snow chains is 50 km/h. Listen for noises. If you hear unusual sounds or feel unstable, you should stop and check the chains. This sign has nothing to do with vehicles that have chains.

2.4.41-102.question_text: Which traffic sign refers to the permissible total weight?
2.4.41-102.comment: If the weight in tons 't' is shown on the main sign, it refers to the actual weight of the vehicle. If there's a picture of a vehicle with an additional sign, it refers to the permissible total weight, including trailers and towing vehicles.

2.4.41-103.question_text: Which traffic sign refers to the actual weight?
2.4.41-103.comment: If the weight in tons 't' is shown on the main sign, it refers to the actual weight of the vehicle. If there's a picture of a vehicle with an additional sign, it refers to the permissible total weight, including trailers and towing vehicles.

2.4.41-104.question_text: Which vehicles are not allowed to drive on a road marked like this?

options.text: Actual axle load exceeds 2 t
Permissible axle load exceeds 2 t
Permissible total weight does not exceed 2 t

2.4.41-104.comment: This traffic sign prohibits vehicles from using the road if they exceed the weight specified on the sign. The weight refers to the actual axle load, which must not be exceeded. The red circle on the sign always indicates a prohibition.

2.4.41-105.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: A ban for vehicles whose width including load exceeds 2 m
A road width of 2 m
A required side distance of at least 2 m from other vehicles

2.4.41-105.comment: The sign 'Prohibition for vehicles over the specified width including load' indicates road narrowing and bottlenecks ahead. The road is not passable for vehicles that are wider than what's indicated on the sign, which in this case is 2 m.

2.4.41-106.question_text: Which vehicles can cause serious accidents if this traffic sign is ignored?

options.text: Length 8 m, width 2.5 m, height 4 m
Length 10 m, width 3.9 m, height 3 m
Length 4 m, width 2.5 m, height 2.5 m

2.4.41-106.comment: This traffic sign targets trucks and warns about height-restricted passages – like tunnels, bridge structures, or high-voltage overhead lines from trams. The height limit is shown by the black triangles, which is 3.8 m here. If a vehicle taller than 3.8 m ignores this sign, it can lead to serious accidents. The truck could get caught in the overhead lines or stuck in the underpass. Length and width are not relevant.

2.4.41-107.question_text: Which vehicles are not allowed to drive on a road marked like this?

options.text: Car with a trailer, total length of the train 11 m
Tractor with trailer, total length of the train 12 m
Truck with a length of 9 m including load

2.4.41-107.comment: The red circle on the traffic sign always indicates a prohibition. Vehicles whose actual length exceeds 10 m are not allowed to use this road. Also, vehicles with trailers that have a total length exceeding 10 m cannot continue on this road. This indicates road conditions that are not passable for longer vehicles.

2.4.41-108.question_text: Which vehicles can you overtake at this traffic sign?

options.text: No vehicles
Single-track vehicles
Multi-track vehicles

2.4.41-108.comment: You can't overtake any vehicles, whether they're single-track or multi-track.

2.4.41-109.question_text: Which motor vehicles does this marked overtaking ban apply to?

options.text: Buses
Single-track motor vehicles
Cars without trailers

2.4.41-109.comment: This sign prohibits overtaking for motor vehicles with a permissible total weight over 3.5 tons. It also applies to buses and cars WITH trailers.

2.4.42-001.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: End of the highway
End of the main road
Temporary closure of the highway

2.4.42-001.comment: This sign is located at the end of the highway.

2.4.42-002.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: End of the main road
End of the highway
Prohibition for motor vehicles

2.4.42-002.comment: This sign marks the end of a main road. From here, the recommended speed no longer applies. It doesn't indicate a prohibition for motor vehicles.

2.4.42-004.question_text: What do these traffic signs indicate?

options.text: The number of a highway
The distance to the next gas station
The number of a European road

2.4.42-004.comment: A white number on a blue background with a white border indicates the number of the highway you're currently on.

2.4.42-005.question_text: What does the number '26' on this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: Highway exit number 26
Distance from the exit to Düsseldorf-Benrath

2.4.42-005.comment: All highway exits are numbered for better orientation. As a driver, you can recognize exit number 26. These numbers also appear on road maps, atlases, and common navigation devices.

2.4.42-006.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: A diversion for highway traffic
A subway station
Federal road 22

2.4.42-006.comment: This traffic sign indicates a diversion for highway traffic. It's set up, for example, in case of a traffic jam. If you follow the diversion, you'll get back on the highway.

2.4.42-101.question_text: What applies after this traffic sign?

options.text: Overtaking can't be announced by honking
Parked cars can be secured with the parking light
At night, you can drive with parking lights

2.4.42-101.comment: Drivers recognize from this sign that the rules for traffic in built-up areas apply. You can't announce overtaking by honking here, as that's only allowed outside built-up areas. It's generally prohibited to drive with parking lights. Parked cars can be secured with the parking light.

2.4.42-102.question_text: How can vehicles up to 2.8 t total weight be parked here?

options.text: Cars as shown in the picture
Caravans as shown in the picture
Small cars can also park sideways

2.4.42-102.comment: This traffic sign tells drivers that vehicles up to 2.8 t total weight can only be parked as shown in the picture. Smaller cars must also follow this parking rule.

2.4.42-103.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: - Hydrogen filling station
- Natural gas filling station
- Autogas filling station

2.4.42-103.comment: The square traffic sign with a blue border indicates that there's a filling station nearby for hydrogen-powered vehicles. These cars are still relatively expensive but are considered the vehicles of the future.

2.4.42-104.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: - Natural gas filling station
- Hydrogen filling station
- Autogas filling station

2.4.42-104.comment: This traffic sign alerts drivers to a natural gas filling station where they can refuel their natural gas-powered vehicle. The abbreviation CNG stands for Compressed Natural Gas.

2.4.42-105.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: - Autogas filling station
- Natural gas filling station
- Hydrogen filling station

2.4.42-105.comment: The sign shows LPG, which stands for Liquefied Petroleum Gas, or autogas. This sign tells drivers that there's an autogas filling station here.

2.4.42-106.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: A charging station for electric vehicles
Explosion risk at a filling station due to electrical devices
The possibility to charge mobile phones

2.4.42-106.comment: You see a plug with a cable on the sign. It indicates a nearby charging station for electric vehicles like electric cars, e-bikes, or electric scooters. You can charge your electric vehicle there.

2.4.42-107.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: A parking lot connected to public transport ('Park + Ride')
A filling station with a car wash ('Care + Clean')
A vehicle rental with a repair shop ('Breakdown service + Repair')

2.4.42-107.comment: The P + R sign on a blue background stands for 'Park and Ride'. It marks a parking lot that connects to public transport.

2.4.43-002.question_text: You need help on the highway. What information does the arrow on the post give you?

options.text: Next emergency call box in the direction of the arrow
Next parking lot in the direction of the arrow
Next exit in the direction of the arrow

2.4.43-002.comment: Arrows on the posts at the side of the highway point towards the nearest emergency call box. If you need help, follow the arrows to reach an emergency call box quickly.

2.5.01-007.question_text: Why should you avoid sharp acceleration?

options.text: Because the noise bothers others
Because it causes more tire wear
Because it puts a lot of stress on the rear brake

2.5.01-007.comment: Sharp acceleration creates extra noise for other road users. It can damage your vehicle with high revs and cause more wear on the tires. The environment also suffers. The rear brake isn't affected more or less by acceleration.

2.5.01-011.question_text: What happens when you use winter tires in the summer months?

options.text: - fuel consumption
- tire wear
- driving stability

2.5.01-011.comment: Every driver should know that winter tires are designed for cold weather and snowy roads. Using them in summer reduces driving stability, leads to more tire wear, and increases fuel consumption.

2.5.01-012.question_text: Which vehicles are allowed to enter the designated environmental zone?

options.text: Vehicles with a green emissions sticker
Motorcycles
Vehicles that meet the requirements for a green emissions sticker, even if they don't have one

2.5.01-012.comment: The additional sign shows which vehicles with which sticker can enter. Motorcycles can enter in any case.

2.5.01-013.question_text: You want to wash your vehicle. Where should you do this for environmental protection?

options.text: At a car wash
In a parking lot
On a public street

2.5.01-013.comment: You should always wash your vehicle at a car wash. They properly dispose of the dirty water. If you wash your car on the street or in a parking lot, that water goes untreated into the ground.

2.5.01-014.question_text: What significantly increases your vehicle's fuel consumption?

options.text: The seat heater
The air conditioning
The navigation system

2.5.01-014.comment: When you turn on the seat heater or air conditioning, it uses a lot of energy and your fuel consumption goes up significantly. Compared to these, navigation systems use relatively little power.

2.5.01-016.question_text: What are the effects of driving at high speeds in vehicles with combustion engines?

options.text: Fuel consumption increases
Emissions increase
Noise level decreases

2.5.01-016.comment: Keep in mind that driving fast leads to high fuel consumption and higher emissions. It also creates more noise, not less.

2.5.01-018.question_text: Why does an environmentally conscious driving style also improve traffic safety?

options.text: You drive predictably
You avoid high speeds
You can only drive slowly with alternative fuels

2.5.01-018.comment: You can drive fast with alternative fuels too. But you drive environmentally friendly when you avoid high speeds and drive predictably, which helps you avoid sudden braking and starting.

2.5.01-106.question_text: What increases your car's fuel consumption?

options.text: Roof racks or ski holders
Carrying unnecessary items
Too high tire pressure

2.5.01-106.comment: You can expect higher fuel consumption if you add roof racks or ski holders or load your vehicle with unnecessary items. However, high tire pressure doesn't really affect fuel consumption, even though it should generally be avoided.

options.text: Keep tire pressure at recommended levels
Remove roof racks or ski holders
Don't drive in the highest gear

2.5.01-107.comment: Extra weight and attachments like roof racks increase fuel consumption, so take them off when not in use. You save fuel by driving at lower RPMs: shift gears early. Turning off the air conditioning also saves fuel, as does keeping tire pressure at the manufacturer's recommended levels, since low pressure increases rolling resistance.

options.text: By driving in 4th or 5th gear in towns
By driving at high engine RPMs
By driving at high speeds

2.5.01-111.comment: Driving at high RPMs creates more noise than driving at lower RPMs. In built-up areas, you should drive in the highest gear possible to keep noise to a minimum. Avoid starting off at high RPMs with squealing tires.

2.5.01-117.question_text: Where should you place the fine dust sticker to mark low-emission vehicles?

options.text: Clearly visible on the inside of the windshield
Clearly visible on the outside of the windshield
Clearly visible on the inside of the rear window

2.5.01-117.comment: As a driver, you need to make sure the fine dust sticker for your low-emission vehicle is clearly visible on the inside of your windshield.

2.5.01-119.question_text: Where can you store your luggage to avoid unnecessarily increasing fuel consumption?

options.text: In the trunk
Behind the front seats
On the roof rack

2.5.01-119.comment: You should ideally only store your luggage in the trunk of your car. Using a roof rack creates a lot of air resistance, which often leads to a significant increase in fuel consumption.

2.5.01-121.question_text: What measure can contribute to environmentally friendly driving?

options.text: Participating in a practical training for fuel-efficient driving
Using electric vehicles
Carpooling

2.5.01-121.comment: If possible, form carpools to reduce the number of vehicles on the road. Training can help you learn a fuel-efficient driving style. Electric vehicles produce no emissions, making them especially eco-friendly.

2.5.01-122.question_text: How can you save fuel when driving a car with an automatic transmission?

options.text: Avoid using 'kick-down' when starting
Use the Eco mode while driving
Turn off the engine when going downhill

2.5.01-122.comment: Accelerating too hard leads to high fuel consumption. If available, drive in Eco mode. The car adjusts its acceleration to reduce fuel consumption.

2.5.01-123.question_text: Which cars driving in a designated environmental zone are required to display a fine dust sticker?

options.text: - Gasoline engine
- Diesel engine
- Electric motor

2.5.01-123.comment: In general, all cars in a designated environmental zone must display a fine dust sticker. Exceptions include things like construction machinery, ambulances, etc.

2.5.01-124.question_text: What effect can listening to very loud music while driving have?

options.text: Signals from other traffic won't be heard
Other road users will be disturbed
The driver's reaction time improves

2.5.01-124.comment: Loud music can drown out warning signals and other sounds from other road users. It can also disturb and endanger other drivers. The driver's reaction time worsens due to loud music and decreased concentration.

2.5.01-125.question_text: How does air resistance affect a vehicle's fuel consumption? What has the biggest impact on air resistance?

options.text: The speed you're driving
The number of passengers
The tread depth of the tires

2.5.01-125.comment: The faster you drive, the greater the air resistance acting on your vehicle. Doubling your speed increases air resistance fourfold. Tire tread depth mainly affects rolling resistance, and the number of passengers doesn't directly impact air resistance.

2.5.01-126.question_text: You have to wait because the train barriers are closed. How can you help the environment while waiting?

options.text: By using the start-stop system
By putting the car in first gear
By using the handbrake

2.5.01-126.comment: Using the start-stop system can turn off the vehicle while waiting and easily restart it, minimizing emissions. Using the handbrake doesn't affect the vehicle's emissions.

2.5.01-127.question_text: What increases the range of an electric vehicle?

options.text: Using a high level of energy recovery (regeneration)
Reducing the heating temperature
Short, strong accelerations

2.5.01-127.comment: If you brake lightly, the electric motor brakes and recovers energy. If you brake hard, it uses mechanical brakes and doesn't recover energy. A high regeneration level makes an electric car behave like a combustion engine, so you might need to brake less mechanically. The heating in an electric car is powered directly by the battery, using energy that could be used for driving.

2.5.01-128.question_text: What advantage does recuperation offer in an electric vehicle?

options.text: - increases the range
- protects the brake system
- allows energy recovery from braking

2.5.01-128.comment: Recuperation means 'recovery'. Just like electrical energy is turned into motion, when you brake, the motion energy is converted back into electrical energy and fed back into the battery. This increases the range of the electric vehicle.

2.5.01-207.question_text: How can you contribute to environmental protection when planning your trips?

options.text: - combine multiple destinations into one trip
- form carpools with other drivers
- plan to use public transport instead of your own vehicle

2.5.01-207.comment: For the sake of the environment, drivers should avoid unnecessary trips. So, plan your trips well and form carpools whenever possible to avoid extra journeys. Using public transport is also a positive contribution to active environmental protection.

2.5.01-208.question_text: How do you safely drive down a slope?

options.text: - in a gear where I need to brake less
- in neutral
- with the ignition off

2.5.01-208.comment: When driving down a slope, use engine braking by shifting to a lower gear. This takes the load off the brake system. Never shift into neutral! Neutral disables engine braking, which could cause your brakes to overheat. Plus, if the ignition is off, the brake booster won't work, significantly increasing your braking distance.

2.5.01-209.question_text: Which vehicles can enter an environmental zone without a fine dust sticker?

options.text: All two- and three-wheeled vehicles
All agricultural and forestry tractors
All vehicles with a catalytic converter

2.5.01-209.comment: In an environmental zone, all two- and three-wheeled vehicles and agricultural and forestry tractors can enter without a fine dust sticker. They are exempt from the restrictions of the environmental zone. Having a catalytic converter does not exempt you from needing an environmental sticker.

2.5.01-211.question_text: Why are short trips with a cold engine particularly harmful to the environment?

options.text: - more fuel is consumed
- material wear is greater
- the vehicle battery gets overloaded

2.5.01-211.comment: Short trips with a cold engine usually consume more fuel than trips with a warmed-up engine. That's why they're particularly harmful to the environment. Also, there's more friction with a cold engine, leading to greater material wear.

options.text: By honking to greet someone
By slamming doors hard
By driving with a roof rack

2.5.01-212.comment: Noise that occurs during normal vehicle operation is considered unavoidable. As a driver, you should avoid extra noise, like honking to greet someone or slamming doors. Using a roof rack doesn't create avoidable noise.

2.6.01-003.question_text: How can you tell when your vehicle needs to go for its next main inspection?

options.text: From the inspection sticker on the back license plate
From the entry in the registration certificate part I
From the entry in the vehicle's manual

2.6.01-003.comment: You can tell from the entry in the registration certificate part I and the inspection sticker on the back license plate. The vehicle's manual won't help with this.

2.6.01-106.question_text: You've parked your registered trailer at a campsite during the winter months. What applies regarding the main inspection?

options.text: The date on the inspection sticker must be kept
The date on the inspection sticker is postponed due to the downtime

2.6.01-106.comment: Even if you've parked your trailer at a campsite, you still need to keep the date for the main inspection. Technical issues like rust can occur at any time and become a safety risk if not addressed.

2.6.01-108.question_text: You've bought a 3-year-old car and want to use it privately. The main inspection is new. What is the deadline for the next main inspection?
2.6.01-108.comment: The first main inspection for a car is after three years, and every subsequent inspection is every 2 years.

2.6.02-027.question_text: What documents do you need to carry when driving a vehicle that requires registration?

options.text: Your driver's license
The registration certificate part I (vehicle registration)
The registration certificate part II (vehicle title)

2.6.02-027.comment: As a driver, you always need to have your driver's license and vehicle registration (registration certificate part I) with you. The vehicle title (registration certificate part II) should be kept safely at home, as it's proof of ownership and not needed while driving.

2.6.02-030.question_text: Due to a technical change in your vehicle, the operating permit has expired. What consequences should you expect if you still use the vehicle on public roads?

options.text: A fine
An entry in the driving eligibility register
Loss of my insurance coverage

2.6.02-030.comment: If you use your vehicle on public roads despite the expired operating permit, you lose your insurance coverage because the vehicle is no longer the one that was originally insured. In Germany, insurance is mandatory, so this results in an offense for driving without insurance. If the police stop you, you'll get a fine and might end up with an entry in the driving eligibility register.

2.6.02-036.question_text: After a technical change to your vehicle, an inspection has taken place. What are you required to do?

options.text: Carry and possibly correct the registration certificate part I
Send it to the vehicle manufacturer
Stick it in the designated spot in the registration certificate part II

2.6.02-036.comment: After a technical change to a vehicle, an inspection usually results in a report. However, there can also be an entry in part I of the registration certificate. You must carry the report with you during every drive and show it if requested, like during a police check.

2.6.02-038.question_text: After modifications to your vehicle, an inspection is required. When must this take place?

options.text: Immediately after the modification
At the next inspection
After a request from the registration office

2.6.02-038.comment: The inspection must be done right after the modification.

2.6.03-001.question_text: What’s correct when reversing with a vehicle combination if your view to the rear is blocked?

options.text: If the connection to the guiding person is lost, you must stop
Only when entering a right-of-way street is guidance required
On a business premises, guidance can be waived

2.6.03-001.comment: When reversing with a vehicle combination and your view is limited, you need to ensure you don't endanger other road users. It's best to have someone guide you, even on business premises.

2.6.03-111.question_text: You want to tow a trailer. When do you need to install additional mirrors on your vehicle?

options.text: If you can't observe all essential traffic situations without additional mirrors
If the trailer's loading area exceeds a width of 1.5 m and a height of 1 m
If it's a caravan or an agricultural trailer

2.6.03-111.comment: As a driver, you're responsible for having a clear view from your vehicle. If a trailer blocks your view and the standard mirrors aren't sufficient, you need to add extra mirrors.

2.6.03-112.question_text: You want to tow a braked trailer. Where can you find information or hints about the permissible trailer load of your car?

options.text: In the registration certificate part I of my car
In the registration certificate part I of my trailer
In the insurance policy

2.6.03-112.comment: The information on how much trailer load a towing vehicle can handle is found in the registration certificate (part I) and in the vehicle's operating manual.

2.6.03-113.question_text: You want to attach a trailer to your car. Where can you find the information about the permissible hitch load of your car?

options.text: - Owner's manual
- Registration certificate Part I
- Registration certificate Part II

2.6.03-113.comment: You can find information about the permissible trailer load in Part 1 of the car's registration certificate and in the owner's manual.

2.6.03-114.question_text: You want to tow a trailer. What do you need to consider?

options.text: - Towing vehicle's trailer load
- Hitch load at the trailer coupling
- Payload of the trailer

2.6.03-114.comment: The manufacturer specifies the maximum hitch load, payload, and trailer load. If these values aren't followed, it can affect how the vehicle handles and may lead to an accident.

2.6.03-115.question_text: You're driving with a trailer on a road with potholes. Your vehicle combination is swaying. How should you behave now?

options.text: - Reduce speed to prevent skidding
- Accelerate to keep the vehicle combination stretched
- Steer quickly to prevent skidding

2.6.03-115.comment: By reducing your speed, you can prevent skidding.

2.6.03-116.question_text: How many trailers can you tow behind a car?
2.6.03-116.comment: According to StVZO § 32 a, you can only tow one trailer behind motor vehicles, but not a trailer for transporting people (bus trailer).

2.6.03-406.question_text: A single-axle trailer has a total weight of 600 kg. What must the hitch load be at a minimum?
2.6.03-406.comment: The hitch load is the weight that rests on the towing vehicle's hitch. To find it, you can place a piece of wood or a pipe under the hitch point of the level trailer and put a scale underneath. The scale will show the hitch load. For trailers with a permissible total weight of no more than 3.5 tons, the minimum hitch load must be at least 4% of the trailer's total weight. However, a minimum hitch load of 25 kg is sufficient. In this case, the minimum hitch load is 24 kg. When loading the trailer, you need to make sure not to exceed or fall below the minimum and maximum permissible hitch loads. You can affect the hitch load by shifting the load.

2.6.06-213.question_text: When can you stay in this situation on the left lane?

options.text: - If the total width including load is actually a maximum of 2 m
- If the vehicle is 2 m wide according to Registration Certificate Part I (vehicle registration)

2.6.06-213.comment: The traffic sign indicates how wide your vehicle, including mirrors and load, can be. Make sure the mirrors are included in the measurements in your vehicle documents.

2.6.06-216.question_text: What do you need to consider in this situation?

options.text: After 200 m, the width of the left lane decreases
My vehicle is wider with mirrors than stated in the vehicle documents
For a length of 200 m, the width of the left lane decreases

2.6.06-216.comment: The upper traffic sign shows that the road narrows to the width indicated on the sign. The additional sign informs you that the narrowing starts about 200 meters ahead. You need to add the width of the mirrors to the measurement stated in your vehicle documents. Uneven road surfaces may also require more width. Keep these factors in mind as you proceed.

2.6.07-001.question_text: What do you need to consider when using navigation systems and maps?

options.text: The content can become outdated shortly after purchase
Even current content can differ from reality
All navigation systems can update automatically

2.6.07-001.comment: When using a navigation system, keep in mind that even current content can differ from reality and that the information can become outdated shortly after purchase. There's no guarantee of accuracy, even with automatic updates.

2.6.07-101.question_text: What should you consider when planning a route abroad?

options.text: - Conditions for urban road use apply (like city tolls)
- There are labeling requirements for entering environmental zones
- Speed limits apply

2.6.07-101.comment: Before your trip, find out what regulations apply in the country you're visiting.

2.6.07-220.question_text: What activities can lead to risky distractions while driving?

options.text: Entering an address in a navigation device
Writing a text message
Making a phone call, even with hands-free

2.6.07-220.comment: All options can lead to risky distractions. Entering an address in a navigation device, writing a text message, and making a phone call with hands-free can all take your attention away from driving.

2.7.01-045.question_text: What should you consider when checking tire pressure?

options.text: Load/occupancy of the vehicle
Temperature of the tires
Material of the rims (steel/light alloy)

2.7.01-045.comment: When checking tire pressure, you should also consider the temperature and the load of the vehicle, as these can affect tire pressure. The material of the rim doesn't matter.

2.7.01-047.question_text: What increases the centrifugal force acting on a vehicle when turning?

options.text: Higher speed
Smaller turning radius
Higher tire pressure

2.7.01-047.comment: Speed directly affects the amount of centrifugal force. Your braking distance quadruples when you drive at double the speed. The centrifugal force increases as the turning radius decreases. Tire pressure has no effect on centrifugal force.

2.7.01-058.question_text: You're driving a car with a trailer on a narrow country road in wet conditions and approaching a clear but tight left turn. How do you behave?

options.text: I reduce speed before the turn
I stay in the middle of the lane and accelerate only when back on straight road
I brake only at the apex of the turn

2.7.01-058.comment: Reduce your speed before the turn. Take the weather conditions into account. Remember that centrifugal force increases twice as fast as speed. You should only accelerate again at the apex of the turn.

2.7.01-065.question_text: What do you need to consider when driving a quad?

options.text: Wearing a suitable helmet is mandatory
Quads tend to tip over in tight turns
Driving characteristics are similar to cars

2.7.01-065.comment: Slow down when turning because quads have a high center of gravity and can tip over.

2.7.01-066.question_text: What should you keep in mind when driving a quad?

options.text: Motorcycle protective clothing should be worn
A warning triangle must be carried
The necessary steering forces can be significantly higher than in a car

2.7.01-066.comment: Quads don't have power steering, so steering can be harder than when driving a car.

2.7.01-102.question_text: What changes when towing a caravan?

options.text: The overtaking distance becomes significantly longer
Sudden steering movements increase the risk of skidding
The braking distance becomes significantly shorter

2.7.01-102.comment: When towing a caravan, not only does the risk of skidding increase, but both overtaking and braking distances become longer. This is due to the additional load and the movement of the trailer.

2.7.01-104.question_text: You're driving your car with a trailer on a road with oncoming traffic and want to turn left. What’s especially important when starting again?

options.text: Think about your own vehicle length
Consider the reduced acceleration ability
Warn oncoming traffic with your headlights

2.7.01-104.comment: With a trailer, your acceleration ability is reduced, and you have a different weight and longer overall length. You need to keep this in mind when starting again. You shouldn't warn oncoming traffic with your headlights in this case.

2.7.01-105.question_text: You're driving a car with an unbraked trailer. There's a long, steep downhill. What’s correct?

options.text: If necessary, reduce speed, shift to a low gear in time, be ready to brake
Consider the trailer pushing you
Relieve the car's brakes by frequently disengaging the clutch

2.7.01-105.comment: You should reduce your speed in good time. Shift to the lowest gear possible. This activates the engine brake, which helps with braking. Never disengage the clutch into neutral, as this would make the vehicle go faster.

2.7.01-107.question_text: What do you need to check before driving a car with a caravan?

options.text: If the trailer's lighting system works
If the rear visibility through the mirrors is sufficient
If passengers in the caravan have fastened their seatbelts

2.7.01-107.comment: Caravans limit your rear visibility. So, before driving, you need to check if your mirrors provide enough rear view. You also need to ensure that the lighting system is working.
