2.7.01-108.question_text: You're driving a car with a fully loaded trailer that has no brakes. What’s correct?

options.text: The braking distance will be longer
The reaction distance will be longer
The stopping distance will be shorter

2.7.01-108.comment: Keep in mind that a fully loaded trailer without brakes will increase the braking distance and thus the stopping distance based on the trailer's weight. The reaction distance doesn't change in this case.

2.7.01-109.question_text: You want to attach a single-axle caravan to your car. What do you need to check?

options.text: If the permissible towing weight or the permissible hitch load of the car is exceeded
If additional mirrors need to be installed due to the width of the caravan
If the caravan is approved for carrying passengers

2.7.01-109.comment: The caravan reduces rear visibility. As a driver, you need to check if the existing mirrors provide enough rear view. You might need to add extra mirrors to your car. The towing vehicle and trailer must always be compatible.

2.7.01-110.question_text: You want to start driving with an automatic car (hydraulic converter). What do you need to know?

options.text: You usually need to hold the car with the brake when engaging a gear
The gear selector should only be operated with the engine off
The engine speed must be significantly increased to avoid stalling

2.7.01-110.comment: When you give a 'go' in a vehicle with an automatic transmission while in gear, it tries to move. You can only prevent this by pressing the brake. You can operate the gear selector with the engine on or off.

2.7.01-111.question_text: What should you pay attention to regarding tire pressure?

options.text: Regularly check tire pressure, including the spare tire
Increase tire pressure when heavily loaded according to the manual
Lower tire pressure before long trips

2.7.01-111.comment: Regularly checking tire pressure helps avoid tire damage and can save fuel. If you expose your vehicle to a heavier load, you need to adjust the tire pressure.

2.7.01-112.question_text: After a flat tire, you mounted the spare wheel. What is forbidden when continuing your journey?

options.text: Driving faster than 80 km/h
Driving with the spare wheel longer than necessary
Taking passengers with you

2.7.01-112.comment: Spare wheels are designed differently than regular wheels and are only approved for speeds up to 80 km/h. They have poorer driving characteristics. You should only drive as far as necessary with them. There's no restriction on taking passengers.

2.7.01-115.question_text: What does a rear-wheel-drive car tend to do if you give it too much gas in a curve?

options.text: It tends to skid out at the back
It tends to skid out at the front
It tends to understeer

2.7.01-115.comment: You should always expect that your rear-wheel-drive vehicle will skid out at the back if you give it too much gas in a curve. Oversteering is more likely than understeering.

2.7.01-118.question_text: What advantages does traction control (ASR) offer?

options.text: It prevents the wheels from spinning when starting.
It reduces the risk of sliding sideways on slippery roads when starting.
It prevents the wheels from locking up when braking.

2.7.01-118.comment: Traction control (ASR) stops the vehicle's wheels from spinning, especially during hard acceleration. This helps prevent sliding sideways when starting on slippery surfaces.

2.7.01-120.question_text: You're about to attach a trailer with a ball coupling. What’s correct?

options.text: The coupling must securely enclose the ball head. The safety must click into place.
The electrical connection must be established.
Adjust the support wheel so it can roll during driving.

2.7.01-120.comment: When attaching a trailer with a ball coupling, make sure the coupling securely encloses the ball head and that the safety clicks into place. Also, ensure the electrical connection works. The support wheel should not roll during driving; it needs to be locked in the raised position.

2.7.01-121.question_text: What do you need to do after attaching a single-axle trailer with a surge brake?

options.text: Check the brake function.
Raise the existing support wheel to the highest position.
Hook the breakaway cable to the towing vehicle's coupling.

2.7.01-121.comment: You need to attach the breakaway cable to the towing vehicle's coupling. With a surge brake, the trailer will brake automatically if it disconnects from the towing vehicle. You should also check the brake function. The support wheel should be raised and locked in place during driving.

2.7.01-122.question_text: What do you need to consider when loading a single-axle trailer?

options.text: - axle load
- tongue load
- total weight

2.7.01-122.comment: When loading a single-axle trailer, make sure to keep the total weight within limits and that your load doesn't exceed the allowed axle and tongue load.

2.7.01-123.question_text: You want to park your single-axle trailer (surge brake, 1,000 kg max total weight) on a slope. What do you need to do?

options.text: Engage the parking brake.
Place wheel chocks in front of the wheels.
Lock the reverse gear.

2.7.01-123.comment: You must secure your trailer against rolling away. Engage the parking brake and place wheel chocks in front of the wheels. Typically, these trailers don't have a reverse gear lock.

2.7.01-124.question_text: What dangerous defects can occur on a trailer with surge brakes after a long period of standing?

options.text: The brakes may be ineffective due to rust.
Cable connections may be damaged.
The tire pressure may have increased significantly due to sunlight.

2.7.01-124.comment: If you leave a trailer standing for a long time, weather can cause damage: electrical connections might get damaged, and rust can form on the brakes. However, sunlight doesn't significantly increase tire pressure, so that’s not a dangerous defect.

2.7.01-125.question_text: What do you need to consider when loading a trailer?

options.text: - must be securely stored.
- can extend up to 1 m beyond the reflectors without additional marking.
- can extend up to 1 m beyond the towing vehicle at the front.

2.7.01-125.comment: Always ensure your load is secured properly. To avoid endangering yourself and other road users, you need to maintain clear visibility and full control of your vehicle. The load must be marked at the back and can extend a maximum of 50 cm at the front.

2.7.01-127.question_text: Why shouldn't you drive down a long, steep slope with the clutch pressed?

options.text: Because the engine braking effect can't be used.
Because it causes unnecessary wear on the brakes.
Because then the brake booster can't work.

2.7.01-127.comment: If you press the clutch while going down a slope, the engine brake won't work, and you'll have to rely more on the regular brakes. This can lead to overheating and increased wear on the brakes.

2.7.01-130.question_text: You need to brake suddenly in a curve on a wet road. What are the special features of a vehicle with anti-lock braking system (ABS)?

options.text: Steering control is maintained longer.
The vehicle always remains stable.
The vehicle can't skid out of the curve.

2.7.01-130.comment: On wet roads, ABS prevents the wheels from locking up and shortens the braking distance. It also helps maintain steering control for a longer time while braking. However, on gravel or snow, the braking distance can be significantly longer.

2.7.01-131.question_text: How do the cornering characteristics of a vehicle combination (car with a trailer) affect turning?

options.text: - can swing out.
- can cut the corner.
- usually follows the car's path.

2.7.01-131.comment: Even with careful driving, the trailer might cut the corner or swing out. Drivers need to be cautious to avoid endangering others.

2.7.01-133.question_text: What can limit the function of a lane-keeping assistant?

options.text: A dirty road
Missing road markings
Missing guardrails

2.7.01-133.comment: The lane-keeping assistant warns you if your vehicle drifts out of its lane. Missing road markings and a dirty road can limit this function. Missing guardrails aren't a big deal.

2.7.01-134.question_text: What should you check before driving an electric vehicle?

options.text: Where I can charge the vehicle
How to behave after an accident
Factors affecting the range

2.7.01-134.comment: Before you start driving an electric vehicle, you should definitely check its range. It's usually much lower than that of traditional cars, so you'll need to stop more often to recharge. Also, keep in mind that electric vehicles have more technology inside. While they're generally as safe as regular cars, they have high-voltage cables running through their bodies.

2.7.01-135.question_text: You're planning a long trip with an electric vehicle. What should you consider?

options.text: The availability of charging stations
The battery charging time
The impact of extreme outside temperatures on range

2.7.01-135.comment: When planning a long trip with an electric vehicle, remember that it has a much shorter range compared to traditional cars. Plus, the battery capacity can be affected by outside temperatures.

2.7.01-136.question_text: What should you keep in mind when charging electric vehicles?

options.text: Charging time depends on the power outlet
Charging should only be done with manufacturer-approved cables
You can charge at any gas station

2.7.01-136.comment: When charging electric vehicles, you need to know that you can't charge them at just any gas station. Only use cables approved by the manufacturer. The charging time varies depending on the power outlet.

2.7.01-137.question_text: What distinguishes electric vehicles from combustion engine vehicles?

options.text: - lower engine noise
- no direct emissions
- lower air resistance

2.7.01-137.comment: Electric vehicles are almost silent. They have no direct emissions. Air resistance depends on the shape of the vehicle, not the type of engine.

2.7.01-138.question_text: You're driving an electric vehicle in a residential area. What should you expect due to your low noise levels?

options.text: Pedestrians may not notice me or notice me late
Cyclists ahead may turn left without looking back
Following vehicles may tailgate too closely

2.7.01-138.comment: When you're driving an electric vehicle, you're almost silent, so other road users might not hear you. This is especially risky for cyclists, who might turn without looking because they can't hear your engine.

2.7.01-139.question_text: You're driving a vehicle with an Anti-lock Braking System (ABS). How do you achieve the shortest braking distance?

options.text: - suddenly and with maximum pedal force
- gently and then increasingly harder
- multiple short presses with maximum pedal force

2.7.01-139.comment: For an emergency stop, the shortest braking distance is achieved by braking suddenly and with maximum pedal force. Short or gentle braking won't give you the desired effect.

2.7.01-141.question_text: You're driving very fast into a tight curve. What can happen if you suddenly need to brake hard?

options.text: - you lose traction
- you skid out of the curve
- you stay stable with stability control at all times

2.7.01-141.comment: If you're speeding into a tight curve and brake hard, you'll lose traction and skid out of the curve due to centrifugal force.

2.7.01-142.question_text: What can cause your vehicle to skid in curves?

options.text: Sharp steering movements
Driving too fast
Light acceleration at the curve exit

2.7.01-142.comment: Sharp steering movements can cause your vehicle to skid in curves. Driving too fast can also lead to this. Make sure to adjust your speed when going through curves.

2.7.01-143.question_text: The lane-keeping assistant warns you with sounds, vibrations, or visual signals. What could be the reason for this?

options.text: My vehicle is getting close to the side road marking
My vehicle is too close to the car in front
Another vehicle is overtaking me with too little space

2.7.01-143.comment: If you drift out of your lane, the lane-keeping assistant detects this by noticing you're getting close to the road marking. The total weight must not be exceeded.

2.7.01-144.question_text: In which situation can the lane-keeping assistant help you with steering intervention?

options.text: - on highways
- on country roads
- in narrow construction zones with poor markings

2.7.01-144.comment: On highways and country roads, the lane-keeping assistant can help with steering because the markings are clearly visible. In construction zones with poor markings and narrow lanes, it can't assist effectively since it might not recognize the markings correctly.

2.7.01-145.question_text: In which driving task can the lane-keeping assistant support the driver with steering intervention?

options.text: When driving straight
When turning
When overtaking

2.7.01-145.comment: With good road markings, the lane-keeping assistant can help keep your vehicle straight on the road. When turning, you cross lanes and markings, so the assistant can't intervene. Also, when overtaking, you signal to the assistant by using your turn signal that you're intentionally crossing the lane marking, so it won't intervene during that.

2.7.01-146.question_text: What can affect the function of the lane-keeping assistant with steering intervention?

options.text: Weather conditions
The condition of the road markings
Additional road markings in construction areas

2.7.01-146.comment: If the road markings are in poor condition, the lane-keeping assistant can't tell where the lane is. Additional markings in construction areas can confuse it about which lane to follow. Weather conditions can also affect the assistant's sensors, and water or snow can distort the markings.

2.7.01-147.question_text: Under what condition does the lane-keeping assistant with steering intervention work best?

options.text: With clear road markings
With snow remnants on the road
With additional construction markings

2.7.01-147.comment: The lane-keeping assistant works best with clear road markings. Poor or additional markings in construction zones can prevent it from intervening correctly. Weather conditions can also impact the assistant's sensors, and snow can distort the markings.

2.7.01-149.question_text: How can driver assistance systems support you?

options.text: - warn me of dangers
- help me with driving tasks
- automatically intervene in critical traffic situations

2.7.01-149.comment: In critical traffic situations, driver assistance systems can react quickly and automatically intervene by steering or braking, etc. If there's a danger, they can warn you with lights, sounds, and vibrations. They can also assist you with driving tasks, like keeping you in your lane.

2.7.01-150.question_text: What could happen if you accelerate too much in a curve with a front-wheel-drive car?

options.text: - lose grip at the front axle
- have limited steering ability
- lose grip at the rear axle

2.7.01-150.comment: If you accelerate too much in a curve with a front-wheel-drive car, it can lose grip at the front axle. The front tires lose traction on the road, and your vehicle won't steer anymore; it will just go straight and skid out.

2.7.01-151.question_text: Under what condition can an active lane change assistant perform a lane change?

options.text: - it has detected a clearly marked road with multiple lanes
- it has detected no vehicles in the relevant safety area
- it has detected a sufficient gap in oncoming traffic

2.7.01-151.comment: For an active lane change, the assistant first needs to detect a marked road with multiple lanes. It will only perform a lane change if it doesn't detect any vehicles in the relevant safety area.

2.7.01-152.question_text: Your vehicle is equipped with an active lane-keeping assistant. What information can be displayed on the status indicator of this system?

options.text: - is on
- is off
- has a malfunction

2.7.01-152.comment: The system must be able to show whether it's on, off, or has a malfunction. This is important information for the driver.

2.7.01-153.question_text: Your vehicle is equipped with a lane-keeping assistant. In which situation can this system help you?

options.text: - unintentionally leaving the lane
- exceeding the maximum speed limit
- driving too fast through ruts

2.7.01-153.comment: The lane-keeping assistant helps you stay in your lane. It warns you when you unintentionally leave the lane.

2.7.01-154.question_text: You're using the lane-keeping assistant in your vehicle. It warns you with a signal while driving. What could be the reason for this?

options.text: I forgot to use my turn signal when changing lanes
I'm unintentionally leaving my lane
I'm not keeping the minimum distance to the vehicle in front

2.7.01-154.comment: If you unintentionally leave your lane, the lane-keeping assistant will warn you. If you forget to signal when changing lanes, the assistant sees this as an unintentional lane departure and alerts you.

2.7.01-155.question_text: You're using the lane-keeping assistant while driving. The system doesn't react when you leave the lane. What could be the reason?

options.text: Insufficient road lighting
Heavy precipitation
Missing lane markings

2.7.01-155.comment: Missing lane markings, insufficient road lighting, and heavy precipitation can affect the sensors of the lane-keeping assistant, making it hard to reliably detect the lane.

2.7.01-156.question_text: Your vehicle is equipped with a lane change assistant without steering intervention. A warning light is on in the left side mirror while driving. What does this warning light indicate?

options.text: There's another vehicle in the monitoring area
A lane change to the left is not allowed right now
A lane change to the left can be done safely now

2.7.01-156.comment: If there's a vehicle in the monitoring area, the warning light in the side mirror will signal this.

2.7.01-157.question_text: You're using the active lane-keeping assistant while driving. How can you manually override this driver assistance system in case it intervenes?

options.text: By counter-steering
By using the turn signal
By accelerating

2.7.01-157.comment: You can override the lane-keeping assistant's intervention by counter-steering or using the turn signal.

2.7.01-158.question_text: In which situation can an active lane change assistant be useful?

options.text: - highways
- highway-like roads
- roads without markings

2.7.01-158.comment: On highways or highway-like roads, lane markings are clear and the roads are usually straight. This is where an active lane change assistant is helpful.

2.7.01-159.question_text: You want to overtake and have initiated a lane change using the active lane change assistant. What's correct?

options.text: The system will carry out the lane change on its own
I need to monitor the lane change
The system always maintains all safety distances on its own

2.7.01-159.comment: The active lane change assistant can carry out the lane change after initiation on its own. However, you always need to monitor it, as safety distances may not always be maintained automatically.

2.7.01-160.question_text: Which driver assistance system do you need to activate manually if you want support in certain situations?

options.text: The active parking assistant
The adaptive cruise control (ACC)
The emergency braking assistant

2.7.01-160.comment: The active parking assistant and adaptive cruise control (ACC) are not considered safety-critical assistants. Therefore, you can activate them manually.

2.7.02-020.question_text: In which cases is a brake test essential?

options.text: When taking over another vehicle
After a vehicle has been parked for a long time
After every oil change

2.7.02-020.comment: A brake test is essential whenever a vehicle has not been used for a long time or when you're taking over a different vehicle. An oil change does not affect the braking system.

2.7.02-027.question_text: Why does a rusted exhaust system need to be repaired immediately?

options.text: Because of noise disturbance
Because parts of the exhaust can fall onto the road
Because the engine might overheat

2.7.02-027.comment: You need to repair a rusted exhaust system right away because parts can fall onto the road, which can endanger other road users. Plus, rusty exhaust parts create unnecessary noise. A rusted exhaust system doesn't affect the engine temperature.

2.7.02-033.question_text: Your vehicle's brake light isn't working. What could be the cause?

options.text: The corresponding fuse is faulty
The bulb is defective
The brake fluid level is too low

2.7.02-033.comment: A working brake light is crucial for participating in traffic. If you notice a problem with your vehicle, you should replace the faulty parts right away. Possible causes include a blown bulb or a broken fuse.

2.7.02-034.question_text: What should you do if the oil pressure warning light doesn't go off after starting the engine?

options.text: I turn off the engine immediately
I check the engine oil level
I keep driving until the next oil change

2.7.02-034.comment: To avoid engine damage, you should turn off the engine immediately and check the oil level.

2.7.02-037.question_text: You hit a curb hard with a wheel. What should you consider?

options.text: The vehicle should be checked at a workshop
The vehicle's handling may worsen
The tire may slowly lose air

2.7.02-037.comment: If you've hit a hard obstacle, you should have the tires and rims checked for possible damage to ensure safe driving. If the wheel was damaged in the impact, it could negatively affect the vehicle's handling. Even if the tire looks fine, it might still slowly lose air.

2.7.02-038.question_text: Your vehicle's tail light isn't working. What could be the cause?

options.text: The corresponding fuse is faulty
The bulb is defective
The high beam switch is broken

2.7.02-038.comment: A blown fuse or a defective bulb could be the reason for a tail light not working.

2.7.02-107.question_text: The brake on your car is working unevenly. What can happen when you brake?

options.text: The vehicle can skid sideways
Longer braking distance
ABS failure

2.7.02-107.comment: If the brake is working unevenly, it can seriously affect how the car handles. The vehicle might skid into adjacent lanes or lose control. The braking distance will also increase. However, the ABS will still function.

2.7.02-109.question_text: You can press the brake pedal all the way to the floor. Only after several presses does the pedal feel firmer. What should you do?

options.text: Stop the vehicle immediately
Get the brakes repaired
Just adding brake fluid is enough

2.7.02-109.comment: If you can press the brake pedal to the floor and it only gets firmer after pumping it several times, there's air in the brake system. This means the brakes need immediate maintenance and repair. You can't continue driving. Just adding brake fluid won't fix the problem.

2.7.02-117.question_text: The windshield washer system isn't working. What could be the reason?

options.text: No water in the reservoir
Blown fuse
Clogged nozzles

2.7.02-117.comment: If the windshield washer system isn't working, it could be due to clogged nozzles or a blown fuse. It's also possible that there's no water left in the reservoir, which would cause the system to fail.

2.7.02-118.question_text: There's not enough water coming from the windshield washer nozzles. What could be the cause?

options.text: Nozzles are partially clogged
Water pump is defective
Too much water in the reservoir

2.7.02-118.comment: If not enough water is coming from the nozzles, it might be because they're partially clogged. A defect in the water pump could also be the reason for the windshield washer's malfunction. Having too much water isn't a possible cause.

2.7.02-119.question_text: What could be the reason if the windshield wipers aren't cleaning properly?

options.text: Wiper blades are worn out
Oil film on the windshield
Defective windshield heater

2.7.02-119.comment: If the windshield wipers aren't cleaning well, it could be due to an oil film on the glass. Worn-out wiper blades can also affect their performance. A defect in the windshield heater won't have any impact.

2.7.02-127.question_text: What effect does steering while stationary have on your vehicle?

options.text: It can damage the tire tread
It puts a lot of stress on the front axle
It makes steering easier

2.7.02-127.comment: Steering while stationary can damage the tire tread. It puts a lot of stress on the front axle, so you should avoid it. Steering doesn't become easier.

2.7.02-128.question_text: When should you have your car's braking system checked?

options.text: When the brake warning light comes on while driving
When my car doesn't stay in line while braking
When an emergency stop has been made with my car

2.7.02-128.comment: The brake warning light indicates a problem with the braking system. If it lights up while driving, you should have the vehicle checked immediately. If the car pulls to one side while braking, it can't stay in line. Get the braking system checked.

2.7.02-129.question_text: While driving, you notice your car pulls strongly to the left when braking. What should you do?

options.text: Have my car checked at a workshop immediately
Just drive slowly
Only use the handbrake to brake

2.7.02-129.comment: If your vehicle behaves unusually, you should always go to a workshop immediately. This can help prevent accidents. Since there's clearly something wrong with your brakes, avoid situations where you need to brake hard. Using the handbrake can cause your car to skid, which you should never do while driving.

2.7.02-130.question_text: Your vehicle is noticeably harder to steer than usual. What should you do?

options.text: I have the vehicle checked at a workshop immediately
I pay attention to this steering behavior on future drives
I reduce the tire pressure at the front axle

2.7.02-130.comment: If your vehicle behaves unusually, you should always go to a workshop right away. Continuing to drive poses too much risk, putting you and other road users in danger.

2.7.02-131.question_text: You notice that the tires on the front axle of your vehicle are unevenly worn. What should be checked?

options.text: The suspension settings
The tire pressure
The shock absorbers

2.7.02-131.comment: Uneven tire wear can have several causes. You should check the tire pressure. A faulty shock absorber or incorrect suspension settings can lead to uneven wear, and both should be checked at a professional workshop.

2.7.02-132.question_text: While driving, your vehicle pulls to the right. What should you do?

options.text: I check the tire pressure and go to a workshop if needed
I only observe the steering behavior on future drives
I try to improve the driving behavior by braking hard

2.7.02-132.comment: If your vehicle pulls to the right while driving, it could indicate incorrect tire pressure. Check it and go to a workshop if necessary. Braking hard won't improve the driving behavior; it just makes driving riskier and could endanger you and others. If your vehicle behaves unusually, always go to a workshop immediately.

2.7.02-133.question_text: When should you have your car checked at a workshop?

options.text: For the suspension
For the steering system
For the paintwork

2.7.02-133.comment: If you notice issues with your suspension or steering system, you should go to a workshop immediately. These problems can be very dangerous for you and others, affecting your vehicle's handling and safety.

2.7.02-134.question_text: The indicator light for the turn signal is blinking much faster than usual. What could be the cause?

options.text: A bulb is defective
The fuse is defective
The hazard lights are on

2.7.02-134.comment: A fast-blinking indicator light usually means a bulb is out. You can see this faster blinking in the vehicle's cockpit, so you can notice it even while driving.

2.7.02-135.question_text: When should you have your car checked in a workshop?

options.text: When there are constant noises while braking
When the airbag warning light doesn't go off after starting the engine
When you need to constantly steer against while driving straight

2.7.02-135.comment: You should have your car checked if the airbag warning light doesn't turn off shortly after starting the engine. This could mean there's an issue with the airbag or seatbelt system. Constant noises while braking might indicate damage to the braking system. Normally, your car should drive straight without you having to hold the steering wheel tightly. If you have to constantly steer against to keep it straight, you should get it checked in a workshop.

2.7.02-136.question_text: While accelerating, you notice the steering wheel is 'shaking'. What should you do?

options.text: - Check the front wheels for damage
- Check the wheel fastening of the front wheels
- Check the steering wheel fastening

2.7.02-136.comment: If the steering wheel shakes while accelerating, you should take a closer look at the front wheels. Start by checking the front wheels for any damage, then see if they're properly secured.

2.7.03-101.question_text: What can happen if there's too little coolant in the engine?

options.text: - can lead to engine damage
- can lead to engine overheating
- can increase fuel consumption

2.7.03-101.comment: Too little coolant can cause engine damage and should always be checked by you. Another consequence is that the engine can overheat. Make sure you have enough coolant.

2.7.03-102.question_text: You're driving at walking speed in a traffic jam. When is clutch wear on your manual transmission vehicle the least?

options.text: - drive in a low gear without using the clutch
- repeatedly start and stop
- drive slowly with a slipping clutch

2.7.03-102.comment: Fully engage the clutch to avoid unnecessary wear. Choose a gear that allows you to roll without using the clutch or gas.

2.7.04-002.question_text: What is the role of engine oil in a combustion engine?

options.text: - for wear protection
- for cooling
- for cleaning

2.7.04-002.comment: Engine oil has various effects on a combustion engine. It provides wear protection, cooling, and cleaning. Make sure you have enough engine oil.

2.7.04-101.question_text: How can you check the engine oil level?

options.text: - Driver information system
- Oil dipstick
- Current fuel consumption display

2.7.04-101.comment: Depending on the vehicle, you can check the engine oil level in different ways. Modern cars can show the oil level in the infotainment system.

2.7.05-001.question_text: What does the manufacturing date '1217' on the tire mean?

options.text: - manufactured in the 12th calendar week of 2017
- manufactured in the 12th month (December) of 2017
- manufactured on 1.2.2017

2.7.05-001.comment: The manufacturing date 1217 means that the tire was made in the 12th calendar week of 2017.

2.7.05-002.question_text: When should you check the tire pressure?

options.text: Regularly when the tires are cold
Immediately after every tire change
Immediately after every drive

2.7.05-002.comment: You should check the tire pressure regularly when the tires are cold and immediately after every tire change. You don't need to check it after every drive.

2.7.05-005.question_text: You're driving with significantly low tire pressure on the road. What’s the consequence?

options.text: The vehicle's steering behavior worsens significantly
Stability in curves dangerously decreases
Tire wear decreases significantly

2.7.05-005.comment: Low tire pressure means a larger area of the tire is in contact with the road. The tire loses its round shape and can't roll properly. So, with significantly low pressure, stability in curves decreases dangerously and steering becomes worse.

2.7.05-101.question_text: What should you pay attention to when changing a tire with a jack?

options.text: The jack should only be placed at the points specified by the vehicle manufacturer
The ground should always be stable and non-slip
The jack should always be placed in the center along the side of the vehicle

2.7.05-101.comment: You should only use the jack at the points specified by the vehicle manufacturer. If you don’t, it could cause damage. The ground should always be stable and non-slip.

2.7.05-102.question_text: You need to remove a defective wheel. In what order should you proceed?

options.text: Secure the vehicle against rolling, place the jack, loosen the wheel nuts, lift the vehicle, remove the wheel nuts
Secure the vehicle against rolling, place the jack, lift the vehicle, loosen the wheel nuts, remove the wheel nuts
Place the jack, secure the vehicle against rolling, loosen the wheel nuts, lift the vehicle, remove the wheel nuts

2.7.05-102.comment: The correct order is: secure the vehicle against rolling, place the jack, loosen the wheel nuts, lift the vehicle, then remove the wheel nuts.

2.7.05-103.question_text: What does the red symbol on the tire mean?

options.text: - is suitable for winter weather conditions
- supports driving characteristics even in snow
- may only be used with snow chains

2.7.05-103.comment: The symbol means this tire is suitable for winter weather and supports driving in snow. Snow chains are not required.

2.7.05-104.question_text: What should you particularly pay attention to when driving with winter tires?

options.text: - not exceed the maximum speed allowed for these tires
- not drive faster than 80 km/h
- drive no faster than when using snow chains

2.7.05-104.comment: With winter tires, you need to make sure you don’t exceed the maximum speed allowed for those tires. You can check this in the speed index.

2.7.05-105.question_text: Your car is equipped with winter tires. What does the speed sticker 'max. 190 km/h' on the dashboard mean?

options.text: - must not be exceeded
- applies only in winter road conditions
- does not apply on dry road conditions

2.7.05-105.comment: You must not exceed the maximum speed of 190 km/h for your winter tires.

2.7.05-106.question_text: What should you check after installing winter tires on your car?

options.text: The tire pressure should be checked according to the manufacturer's specifications
The maximum speed of the tires should be considered
The air pressure should be 0.5 bar lower than the manufacturer's specification for summer tires

2.7.05-106.comment: After installing winter tires, you should check the tire pressure according to the manufacturer's specifications and consider the maximum speed of the tires. This must not be exceeded.

2.7.05-217.question_text: What can happen if the wheel fastenings are not tightened after a wheel change?

options.text: The wheel can be damaged
The wheel can come off the vehicle
The tire can come off the rim

2.7.05-217.comment: If the wheel fastenings are not tightened after a wheel change, the wheel can come off the vehicle during driving due to vibrations. This can cause a serious accident. The wheel cannot come off the rim.

2.7.06-101.question_text: What does an Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Even on slippery roads, the vehicle is braked as effectively as possible
Steering ability is largely maintained while braking
Aquaplaning is prevented

2.7.06-101.comment: An Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking up even during hard braking. The vehicle remains at least somewhat steerable, and the braking distance doesn’t change much on slippery roads. ABS doesn’t prevent aquaplaning, which mainly occurs at high speeds when a water layer forms between the road and the tires.

2.7.06-103.question_text: What advantages does an Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) offer?

options.text: It prevents the wheels from locking during braking
Even with hard braking, steering ability is maintained
Curves can be taken much faster

2.7.06-103.comment: The Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel locking during braking on wet or dirty roads by regulating brake pressure in short intervals. Normal driving characteristics are not affected by ABS.

2.7.06-104.question_text: What advantages does an anti-lock braking system (ABS) offer?

options.text: You can brake hard and swerve at the same time
It prevents the wheels from spinning when starting
It reduces the risk of tipping when braking in curves

2.7.06-104.comment: An anti-lock braking system is especially helpful during hard braking on wet or dirty roads. It prevents the wheels from locking up by adjusting the brake pressure in quick intervals, keeping the vehicle on track. ABS doesn't affect handling in curves. The system that prevents wheel spin when starting is called traction control (ASR), not ABS.

2.7.06-105.question_text: When does the braking effect occur in a trailer with overrun brakes?

options.text: When the trailer runs into the towing vehicle
At the same time as the brake pedal is pressed in the towing vehicle
Before the braking effect occurs in the towing vehicle, to keep the connection tight

2.7.06-105.comment: The braking effect in a trailer with overrun brakes happens when the trailer runs into the towing vehicle. As the name suggests, the trailer's brake is only activated when it pushes against the towing vehicle.

2.7.06-110.question_text: What can happen if you turn off the cruise control too late?

options.text: You might tailgate too closely
You might take a turn too fast
You might exceed the maximum speed limit

2.7.06-110.comment: Turning off the cruise control too late can lead to tailgating. It can also result in taking turns too fast or exceeding the maximum speed limit.

2.7.06-111.question_text: How can a cruise control system assist you?

options.text: By maintaining a constant speed
By promoting fuel-efficient driving
By keeping a minimum distance from the vehicle ahead

2.7.06-111.comment: A cruise control system can help you maintain a constant speed. It can also support fuel-efficient driving.

2.7.06-112.question_text: What should you keep in mind when using an adaptive cruise control system?

options.text: You must stay attentive even after long use of the system
Heavy rain or snow can affect the system
You can override the system at any time using the gas or brake pedal

2.7.06-112.comment: When using an adaptive cruise control system, remember to stay attentive even after using it for a while. Heavy rain or snow can interfere with the system, and you can override it anytime by using the gas or brake pedal.

2.7.06-114.question_text: What advantage does using a cruise control system offer to a driver of a motor vehicle?

options.text: - keeps a set speed constant on flat roads
- relieves the driver from vehicle operation
- adjusts speed to traffic density

2.7.06-114.comment: Cruise control keeps a set speed constant on flat roads and relieves you from having to operate the vehicle as much. It doesn't adjust speed based on traffic density.

2.7.06-115.question_text: In which situation is using an adaptive cruise control system useful?

options.text: - Highways
- Main roads
- Winding roads

2.7.06-115.comment: The adaptive cruise control system monitors the distance to the vehicle ahead and adjusts your speed accordingly. It's useful on highways and main roads.

2.7.06-116.question_text: How can you manually override an activated cruise control system?

options.text: By braking
By accelerating
By steering

2.7.06-116.comment: You can override an active cruise control system by pressing the brake or by accelerating. This means the vehicle will go slower or faster than the set speed.

2.7.06-117.question_text: What function does an adaptive cruise control system perform in motor vehicles?

options.text: - accelerates automatically to a preset speed
- brakes automatically when it detects a slower vehicle ahead
- always maintains the required safety distance from the vehicle ahead

2.7.06-117.comment: The adaptive cruise control system adjusts the vehicle to the speed you set, just like a regular cruise control. It also brakes when it detects slower vehicles ahead. However, it won't brake if it can't see any vehicles, like at night or in heavy rain or fog.

2.7.06-405.question_text: You want to drive with a trailer that has overrun brakes. What do you need to check before starting your trip?

options.text: - Locking of the connection device
- Function of the lighting system
- Attachment of the breakaway cable

2.7.06-405.comment: Make sure to check that the locking mechanism of the overrun brake is secure before starting your trip. Also, check that the entire lighting system works and that the breakaway cable is properly attached.

2.7.08-001.question_text: Why do you need to regularly change the brake fluid according to the manufacturer's guidelines?

options.text: So the braking system stays functional even under high load
To keep the water content in the brake fluid from getting too high
To prevent damage to the braking system components

2.7.08-001.comment: You should regularly change the brake fluid as per the manufacturer's guidelines to ensure the braking system works well under high load, to keep the water content in the brake fluid from getting too high, and to prevent damage to the braking system components.

2.8.01-001.question_text: How long does the probationary period usually last?

options.text: 2 years
1 year
3 years

2.8.01-001.comment: Normally, the probationary period lasts 2 years. However, there are situations where it can be extended up to 4 years.

2.8.01-009.question_text: You're in the probationary period and haven't had any issues so far. What could happen if you don't stop at the sign 'Stop. Give way.' and endanger other road users?

options.text: Order to attend a refresher seminar for new drivers
Entry in the driving aptitude register
Order to retake the theoretical driving test

2.8.01-009.comment: Ignoring the 'Stop. Give way.' sign is a serious violation, an A-violation, which will be recorded in the driving aptitude register. If you commit an A-violation or two less serious violations (B-violations) during the probationary period, you'll have to attend a refresher seminar. You won't need to retake the test.

2.8.01-010.question_text: What is the goal of attending a refresher seminar during the probationary period?

options.text: To develop a more considerate and risk-aware attitude towards traffic
To improve hazard recognition
To reduce points in the driving aptitude register

2.8.01-010.comment: By attending a refresher seminar for new drivers during the probationary period (ASF), you'll learn to analyze your daily driving behavior and sharpen your awareness of dangerous situations. You can't reduce points with this seminar; that's what the driving aptitude seminars (FES) are for.

2.8.01-013.question_text: A new driver has committed several violations during the probationary period. The authority has ordered them to attend a refresher seminar. What should they expect if they don't comply?

options.text: Loss of driving license
Extension of the probationary period by another 3 years
Order for a driving aptitude seminar

2.8.01-013.comment: The probationary period for new drivers lasts 2 years. During this time, strict penalties apply. If you commit an A-violation or two B-violations, you'll be ordered to attend a refresher seminar (ASF). If you don't comply with this order, your driving license will be revoked.

1.7.01-006.question_text: Wet conditions can affect the performance of drum brakes. What should you do then?

options.text: I carefully dry the brake
I apply the brake several times while stationary
I top up the brake fluid

1.7.01-006.comment: A wet drum brake should be driven carefully in order to dry the brake.

1.1.02-201-M.question_text: Why do you have to stop here?

options.text: Because a female pedestrian wants to cross the road from the left
Because a pedestrian wants to cross the road from the right
Because a female cyclist wants to cross the road from the left

1.1.02-201-M.comment: The pedestrian on the left side and a pedestrian in front of the bus (half covered) seem to want to cross the road. So I have to stop. The cyclist continues straight ahead on the sidewalk.

1.1.07-202-M.question_text: Why do you have to brake now?

options.text: Because of the cyclist
Because of the red vehicle
Because of the bus stop

1.1.07-202-M.comment: The cyclist has to switch to the roadway because of the construction work on the sidewalk. The distance between the sidewalk and the tram is so small that overtaking is not possible. I therefore have to brake. There is no tram stop in sight.

1.2.02-201.question_text: You are driving in a built-up area on a bike path that is open to mopeds. What should you expect?

options.text: - doors of parked vehicles being opened suddenly
- turning vehicles overlooking me
- pedestrians using the bike path

1.2.02-201.comment: Even as a moped driver I always have to expect misconduct from other road users. All three answers are correct.

1.2.09-201-M.question_text: Why do you have to wait now?

options.text: Because of the tram
Because of the cyclist
Because of the yellow car

1.2.09-201-M.comment: If you want to turn to the left, you are only allowed to get into line on longitudinally laid rails if no rail vehicle is obstructed. That is why you have to wait.

1.2.11-201-M.question_text: You want to go straight. How should you behave if the red truck starts moving immediately at 'green'?

options.text: I wait and let the truck go first
I give warning signals if necessary
I also start moving immediately

1.2.11-201-M.comment: This is a question only for the class Mofa! So you are riding a Mofa. The truck's acting wrong, but I'm still waiting to avoid an accident. If necessary I give a warning sign.

1.1.02-202-M.question_text: Why do you have to brake now?

options.text: Because of the child
Because of the green car
Because of the cyclist

1.1.02-202-M.comment: The child on the right has already walked in front of the transporter and seems to want to cross the road. You should slow down, in order to be able to stop on time if necessary.

1.1.07-203-M.question_text: What do you have to pay attention to now?

options.text: To the cyclist on the left
To the female cyclist on the right
To the blue car

1.1.07-203-M.comment: I want to turn left, so I have to watch out for the cyclist on the left. The cyclist on the right seems to be going on the road, so I have to watch out for you too. I do not have to pay attention to the parking car.

1.1.07-204-M.question_text: What should you expect in this situation?

options.text: The driver of the yellow car overlooks me
There is rolled gravel on the roadway
The tractor in front of me is turning right

1.1.07-204-M.comment: At the beginning of the video the danger sign 'grit, gravel' was to be seen, therefore you have to expect rolling gravel. The driver of the turning car is obstructed in the view by the tractor and he might overlook me.

1.2.09-202-M.question_text: Why do you have to wait to turn right in this situation?

options.text: Because of the female pedestrian
Because of the female cyclist
Because of the blue car

1.2.09-202-M.comment: StVO 9 Abs. 3: Anyone who wants to turn must allow oncoming vehicles to pass, rail vehicles, bicycles with auxiliary motors, bicycles and miniature electric vehicles even if they are driving in the same direction on or next to the roadway. This also applies to public buses and other vehicles that use marked special lanes. Special attention must be paid to pedestrians; if necessary, maintenance must be carried out.

1.2.09-203-M.question_text: Why are you not allowed to turn now?

options.text: because of the red car
because of the yellow truck
because of the blue tractor

1.2.09-203-M.comment: To my left there is an overtaking car.

1.2.09-204-M.question_text: Why must you wait before turning left in this situation?

options.text: Because of the tram
Because of the red car
Because of the yellow vehicle

1.2.09-204-M.comment: A tramway is approaching from behind. Since you might have to stop in the rail area due to oncoming traffic on the opposite lane, you must not enter the rail area and obstruct the tramway. Since you are on a priority road, you have right of way over traffic coming from the right.

1.2.09-205-M.question_text: Why must you wait before turning left in this situation?

options.text: Because of the motorcycle
Because of the red car
Because of the female cyclist

1.2.09-205-M.comment: The motorcycle behind the oncoming vehicle has right of way and you have to wait. Since you turn in front of the oncoming vehicle you do not have to wait because of this vehicle. "Oncoming vehicles that want to turn left must turn in front of each other, ....". (§ 9 paragraph 4 sentence 2 StVO) Since you are on a priority road, you have right of way over traffic coming from the right.

1.2.11-202-M.question_text: You want to go straight. Where should you position yourself in this situation?

options.text: Right behind the truck
Left behind the truck
Directly behind the motorcycle

1.2.11-202-M.comment: For the truck, visibility to the side and to the rear is often severely restricted and the blind spot is large. Since the truck wants to turn right, the danger of being overlooked is quite high. To avoid a collision, stop on the right behind the truck.

1.2.20-201-M.question_text: How should you behave correctly in this situation?

options.text: I stay behind the tram
I drive past the tram on the right
I overtake the tram on the left

1.2.20-201-M.comment: You stay behind the tramway in order to avoid endangering the passengers getting on and off the tramway. Since you are just before an intersection and cannot see this intersection and oncoming traffic, you must not overtake the tramway on the left.

1.2.37-201-M.question_text: How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: I give way to possible cross traffic
I wait at the stop line for the next green phase
I cross the intersection quickly as 'yellow' is displayed

1.2.37-201-M.comment: If the traffic light is flashing yellow, pay attention to the traffic signs. Here the traffic sign 'Give way!' indicates to the road user that he must give way to possible cross traffic at the crossing.

1.1.07-205-M.question_text: You are driving outside of towns. How should you behave correctly in this situation?

options.text: I only continue after I have convinced myself that the road is clear
I do not need to convince myself that the road is clear, as the cyclist is riding
I must not use the bike lane any further

1.1.07-205-M.comment: This is a question only for the class Mofa! So you are riding a Mofa. I cannot rely on other road users to behave properly and I have to see for myself whether the road is clear. Outside towns and cities, Mofas are allowed to use bike lanes.

1.1.06-201-M.question_text: Why are you not allowed to overtake in this situation?

options.text: Because the overtaking path is not visible
Because I can only drive slightly faster than the cyclists
Because an overtaking ban is signposted

1.1.06-201-M.comment: StVO § 5 Overtaking (2) Overtaking is only permitted to anyone who can see that there is no obstruction to oncoming traffic during the entire overtaking process. Furthermore, overtaking is only permitted to anyone who is driving at a significantly higher speed than the person being overtaken. Since the overtaking path is not visible due to the upcoming right turn, overtaking is not allowed here. When overtaking cyclists, the prescribed lateral distance outside built-up areas is at least 2 meters.

1.1.07-206-M.question_text: Why should you be ready to brake now?

options.text: Because the driver of the brown vehicle might get out
Because the female pedestrian might run onto the road
Because the bus might drive into my lane

1.1.07-206-M.comment: The brown vehicle has just stopped and the driver might get out in a hurry, not paying attention to the traffic. I must therefore be ready to brake. The pedestrian is behind the delivery vehicle and will not run abruptly onto the road. Since there are no parked cars to the right of the bus, there is no reason the bus could drive into my lane.

options.text: because of the cyclist
because of the blue vehicle
because of the yellow car

1.2.09-206-M.comment: A cyclist is coming towards you on the left-hand cycle path, but at the moment he is obscured by the oncoming vehicle. The cyclist and oncoming vehicle have priority. The car turning into the priority road from the left must wait.

1.1.02-052.question_text: Why must you expect that children behave unpredictably in road traffic?

options.text: are easily distracted
often can only partially overview the traffic situation
often cannot determine from which direction a sound comes

1.1.02-052.comment: All three answers are correct. Special consideration must always be given to children in road traffic, as they are often less experienced in traffic than adults due to their physical and mental development. Children are often less able to judge distances and speeds of vehicles than adults and often have a limited field of vision, which puts them at particular risk. In addition, children are often unpredictable and can act quickly and unexpectedly.

options.text: I reduce my speed
I prepare for an emergency stop
I continue driving steadily

1.1.02-138-M.comment: On the sidewalk on the left, the dog has broken away and seems to be running across the road. I immediately reduce my speed and prepare for a possible emergency stop.

1.1.03-007-M.question_text: You are driving after heavy rain. What should you consider in this situation?

options.text: I should maintain a large safety distance from the vehicle in front
I can hardly recognize bumps on the road
Splash water can impair my visibility

1.1.03-007-M.comment: After the heavy rains, deep puddles may have formed on the road. Bumps in the road are difficult to see and the spraying water from the vehicle in front can impair my visibility. Therefore, I increase my safety distance from the vehicle in front.

1.1.07-173.question_text: While driving, a deer crosses the road in front of your vehicle. What should you consider?

options.text: Other animals may follow the deer
The deer may stop in the middle of the road
The deer can be scared away by turning on the high beams

1.1.07-173.comment: Deer often travel in small groups, so I have to expect more animals. Exactly how the deer behaves is unpredictable. It may cross the road quickly, turn around or simply stop on the road. Switching on the high beams is exactly the wrong behaviour, because the deer is blinded by the high beams and stops.

1.1.09-032.question_text: What can the consumption of drugs cause?

options.text: An impairment of concentration
An increase in risk-taking
A misjudgment of speeds

1.1.09-032.comment: All three answers are correct! The use of drugs can have a significant impact on a person's physical and mental state and thus pose a major risk to road participation. Here are some possible effects of drug use on road participation: Drugs such as cannabis or LSD can alter perception and impair the ability to correctly assess dangers in road traffic. Drugs such as cocaine or amphetamines can impair motor skills, which can severely limit driving ability.

1.1.09-033.question_text: Which substance can lead to unfitness to drive when consumed before or during driving?

options.text: Cocaine
Alcohol
Hashish

1.1.09-033.comment: All three answers are correct! The use of drugs or alcohol can have a significant impact on a person's physical and mental condition and can therefore pose a major risk to road use. Important: Drugs can render a person unfit to drive even if taken in small quantities or consumed only once. Because their degradation in the body is unpredictable, it is also difficult to assess the decrease in effectiveness.

1.2.11-007-M.question_text: You want to continue driving straight. What is correct in this situation?

options.text: I let the closed convoy pass
I wait at the stop line
I cross the intersection

1.2.11-007-M.comment: It is obviously a so-called 'closed formation'. This 'closed formation' has the right of way and therefore I wait at the stop line and let the convoy pass.

1.2.37-021.question_text: What applies at this traffic light-controlled intersection with additional signs?

options.text: Cyclists are allowed to turn right even if the light is 'red'
Motor vehicles are allowed to turn right even if the light is 'red'
For cyclists, the direction of travel to the right is prescribed

1.2.37-021.comment: §37 StVO regulates changeable light signs, permanent light signs and the green arrow. At intersections, red means: 'Stop before the intersection'. After stopping, turning right is also permitted on red if a sign with a green arrow on a black background (green arrow) is displayed to the right of the red light. The additional sign 'Cyclists only' restricts the green arrow to cyclists.

options.text: I am allowed to go first
I must let the red car turn
I must let the cyclist pass

1.3.01-044-M.comment: At intersections and junctions without traffic signs, traffic lights or signs from police officers, the person coming from the right always has the 'right of way'. Right before left also applies to cyclists.

1.4.42-009-M.question_text: What does the white marking on the road mean in this situation?

options.text: indicates a waiting obligation due to the right-before-left rule
marks a traffic-calmed area
warns of a poor road condition

1.4.42-009-M.comment: StVO - Annex 3 The sign 342 "Shark's teeth" indicates an obligation to wait. This can exist, for example, at a road junction due to the right-before-left rule.

1.4.42-010-M.question_text: What applies in this situation due to the road marking?

options.text: I must approach the intersection cautiously
I must give way to the red vehicle
I must stop before the road marking

1.4.42-010-M.comment: The road marking is sign 342 "Shark's teeth". It serves to clarify a waiting obligation for vehicle traffic as a result of an existing right before left rule. At this crossing, "right before left" applies. I approach the crossing carefully and, as there is no vehicle coming from the right, I cross the crossing first. I am not obliged to stop at the marking.

2.1.01-008-M.question_text: Why should you allow the truck to change lanes?

options.text: Because the truck driver may not see me
Because I should show consideration for the truck
Because the zipper merge procedure should be applied here

2.1.01-008-M.comment: The truck driver may want to turn left at the next crossing and therefore want to change to the left lane. § 1 Basic rules of the StVO (1) Participation in road traffic requires constant caution and mutual consideration. The truck driver may overlook me, so I am careful, show consideration and let the truck change lanes. A lane narrowing and thus a zip procedure is not indicated.

2.1.02-006-M.question_text: How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: I stop
I continue driving unchanged
I accelerate

2.1.02-006-M.comment: A person wants to cross the road I am turning into. At the moment, however, she is obscured by the construction worker. I stop and let the person cross the road.

2.1.03-124.question_text: Why is overtaking on this snowy road dangerous?

options.text: Because my vehicle can skid
Because the road may be icy in places
Because my visibility may be further impaired

2.1.03-124.comment: The overtaking lane is covered with slush, which can severely impair road grip. In addition, there is the danger that the road under the slush may still be icy. The vehicles to be overtaken can splash slush and water, which impairs visibility.

2.1.06-031-M.question_text: Why must you abort the overtaking maneuver now?

options.text: Because the tractor will turn left
Because the motorcycle will overtake me
Because an overtaking prohibition sign is in sight

2.1.06-031-M.comment: The tractor in front has put on its indicator, clearly signalling that it wants to turn left. The motorbike makes no sign of wanting to overtake me. There is no overtaking sign in sight.

2.1.06-032.question_text: You are driving on a road with one lane for each direction. In front of you is a closed convoy of vehicles. Why should you refrain from overtaking to avoid dangerous situations?

options.text: Because the overtaking distance is significantly larger than with individual vehicles
Because I should not interrupt the closed convoy by merging early
Because I cannot overview the traffic situation in front of the closed convoy

2.1.06-032.comment: All three answers are correct. A closed formation is considered as one vehicle, so I am not allowed to join the formation. Since I have to overtake the closed formation as a whole, the overtaking distance becomes much longer and the traffic situation in front of the closed formation more difficult to survey. To avoid dangerous situations, I should therefore refrain from overtaking.

2.1.07-122.question_text: You are driving on a winding road that is popular with motorcyclists. What should you expect?

options.text: Motorcyclists may encroach into my lane due to their strong lean angle in curves
Motorcyclists cut corners
Motorcyclists overtake me dangerously

2.1.07-122.comment: A winding route that is very popular with motorcyclists. This means that motorcyclists want to have fun on this route. Therefore, I have to expect risky overtaking manoeuvres, cutting corners, etc. All three answers are correct.

options.text: The driver of the yellow truck sees the end of the traffic jam too late
The motorcycle is driving between the rows of vehicles
The blue car is merging in front of me

2.1.08-032-M.comment: The blue car has also reduced its speed considerably and will certainly not pull in in front of me. The motorbike on my left seems to want to pass between the rows of vehicles. In the rear-view mirror, you can see that the yellow truck is approaching very quickly and does not seem to have noticed the traffic jam yet.

2.1.08-102.question_text: Why should you avoid overtaking in the construction area?

options.text: The time savings are often minimal
Vehicles in the right lane may cross the yellow road marking
The accident risk increases significantly

2.1.08-102.comment: All three answers are correct. In this traffic situation, there is neither a speed limit nor an overtaking ban. However, the truck in the right-hand lane has already briefly entered my lane and the slight right-hand bend means that I cannot see the rest of the road. Therefore, I should not overtake here.

2.1.10-103.question_text: When should you interrupt your journey?

options.text: if I want to pick up an object that has fallen in the vehicle
if I notice that my concentration is declining
if I want to activate the cruise control

2.1.10-103.comment: Anyone driving a car must constantly keep an eye on the course of the road, other road users, the control instruments and the rear-view mirror. Only those who drive attentively and with concentration are safe on the road and can make the right decisions quickly. A dropped object or declining concentration are certainly reasons to interrupt the journey. Cruise control is activated in a similar way to the indicator by a short movement of the hand on the steering wheel. The journey does not have to be interrupted.

2.2.04-005.question_text: What minimum safety distance should you maintain outside built-up areas to the vehicle in front?

options.text: Half of the speedometer reading in meters
One third of the speedometer reading in meters
One fifth of the speedometer reading in meters

2.2.04-005.comment: Outside built-up areas, the safety distance should be at least half the speed of the automobile as shown on the speedometer.

2.2.05-020-M.question_text: You want to overtake the vehicle in front of you. What is required for this?

options.text: I must significantly increase my speed
I must indicate my intention to overtake by signaling
I must observe the traffic behind and to the side

2.2.05-020-M.comment: There are some important rules to follow when overtaking on the motorway: Before overtaking, look in the rear-view mirror and side mirror to see if a vehicle is coming from behind and if the left lane is free. Signal the overtaking manoeuvre with the indicator to warn other road users and make it clear that you are changing lanes. Accelerate to an appropriate speed to be able to carry out the overtaking manoeuvre quickly and safely. Keep a sufficient distance from the overtaken vehicle.

2.2.12-109-M.question_text: You want to park in reverse on the right side. What is correct in this situation?

options.text: I pay attention to oncoming traffic before steering
I anticipate vehicles that may be pulling out
I turn on the hazard warning lights

2.2.12-109-M.comment: The hazard warning lights may only be switched on when the vehicle is stationary (§ 15), when towing vehicles (§ 15a) and when others are endangered by the vehicle or must be warned of danger. Parking is certainly no reason to switch on the hazard warning lights. However, I have to watch out for oncoming traffic and for vehicles pulling out.

2.2.18-105.question_text: What is prohibited when using motorways?

options.text: Stopping on the hard shoulder
Reversing
Turning around

2.2.18-105.comment: Turning and reversing are forbidden on the motorway. Likewise stopping – even on the hard shoulder – is also forbidden.

2.2.21-124.question_text: What should be considered when using a seatbelt?

options.text: The seatbelt should not be twisted
The seatbelt should be pulled tight after fastening
A damaged seatbelt must be replaced

2.2.21-124.comment: All three answers are correct! These points are important so that the seat belt protects you from injury in the event of an accident. Make sure that the belt is not twisted. A twisted belt cannot protect you properly in an accident. Put the seat belt on properly. Put the lap belt around your waist and the shoulder belt around your shoulder. Make sure that the belt is tight but not too tight. Check the belt for visible damage or tears before putting it on. If the belt is damaged, it must not be used.

2.2.21-125.question_text: What restricts the function of a three-point seatbelt?

options.text: Wearing a thick winter jacket
Running the belt under both arms
The incomplete engagement of the belt in the buckle

2.2.21-125.comment: All three answers are correct. A thick winter jacket acts like an air cushion, preventing the belt from being tight. If the belt is not fully engaged in the buckle, the buckle may open in an accident. The belt must not rest against the neck or pass under both arms. The correct position is over the shoulder and collarbone.

2.2.21-126.question_text: What should you check before starting your journey?

options.text: if every passenger has fastened their seatbelt
if I can ensure adequate traffic observation
if I have the registration certificate part II with me

2.2.21-126.comment: Before driving off, make sure that safety is not impaired in any way. Visibility must not be obstructed. Objects that could injure the occupants in the event of a collision must be removed or stowed safely before driving off. The driver is responsible for his passengers and must ensure that they are also wearing seat belts. The registration certificate part II does not have to be carried.

2.2.21-127.question_text: What should be considered regarding the desired protective effect of airbags?

options.text: Airbags can only achieve their full function with the correct seating position of the passengers
The deployment space of airbags must not be impaired
Airbags can replace the seatbelt during city driving

2.2.21-127.comment: The best protective effect of the airbags is achieved when the person is in the correct seating position in front of the airbag and the space between the airbag and the person is free of other objects. The seat belt must also always be worn in city traffic.

2.2.21-128.question_text: You want to transport a person in a motor vehicle who must remain in a wheelchair during the journey. What must you consider?

options.text: The motor vehicle must be equipped with a wheelchair space
The wheelchair must be secured with a wheelchair restraint system
The person must be secured with a wheelchair user restraint system

2.2.21-128.comment: § 35 a paragraph 4 a) StVZO stipulates that passenger cars in which wheelchair users are transported seated in a wheelchair must be equipped with wheelchair parking spaces. Each wheelchair space must be equipped with a wheelchair restraint system and a wheelchair user restraint system.

2.2.22-130.question_text: What should you expect when transporting cargo on the roof of your car?

options.text: the car may lean more to the side in curves
it may react more sensitively to crosswinds
it may have increased fuel consumption

2.2.22-130.comment: All three answers are correct. Transporting cargo on the roof increases the vehicle's centre of gravity, which leads to a greater tendency to corner, among other things. At the same time, the surface area of attack increases, making the vehicle more susceptible to crosswinds and increasing fuel consumption.

2.2.22-131.question_text: You are transporting furniture with a van. During a break, you notice that a tie-down strap is severely damaged. Under what condition may you continue driving?

options.text: I have replaced the tie-down strap
I am using other suitable load securing devices
I continue driving at a maximum of 50 km/h

2.2.22-131.comment: Whoever drives a vehicle must also ensure that the vehicle, the train, the team as well as the load and the crew are in accordance with the regulations and that the road safety of the vehicle is not impaired by the load or the crew. This requires that the broken belt is replaced by another belt or securing device and that the journey may only be continued afterwards.

2.2.22-132.question_text: What should be considered when transporting pedelecs on a rear carrier system for the trailer coupling?

options.text: the rear carrier system must be suitable
the drawbar load of the trailer coupling must be suitable
the tyre pressure of the car must be adjusted accordingly

2.2.22-132.comment: All three answers are correct. A pedelec or e-bike weighs on average approx. 25 kg and thus significantly more than a normal bicycle. Therefore, make sure that the rear carrier system and the drawbar load of the trailer coupling are suitable for this heavy load. The tyre pressure of the car must be adjusted accordingly.

2.2.34-103.question_text: What function does the eCall system perform in the event of a serious accident?

options.text: it transmits the position of the motor vehicle
it transmits the time of the accident
it transmits the severity of injuries of the persons in the vehicle

2.2.34-103.comment: An eCall system is an in-vehicle emergency call system that automatically makes an emergency call to a PSAP if the vehicle is involved in a serious accident. The system uses GPS and other sensors to determine the exact location of the accident and transmits this information along with other relevant data such as the number of vehicle occupants, the time and the vehicle identification number to the emergency control centre. This allows the rescue control centre to respond quickly and effectively.

2.2.34-104.question_text: In which situation is a manual activation of the eCall system provided?

options.text: If I witness a serious accident
If a passenger suffers a medical emergency
If my vehicle has a flat tire

2.2.34-104.comment: An eCall system is an in-vehicle emergency call system that automatically sends an emergency call to an emergency call centre if the vehicle is involved in a serious accident. The eCall system can also be triggered manually by pressing the 'SOS button'. This is important, for example, if a passenger has a medical emergency or I witness a serious accident.

2.4.42-109-M.question_text: What is correct in this situation?

options.text: I may drive on the protection lane after I have excluded a danger to cyclists through careful traffic observation
I may only drive on it until I have passed the truck
I may not drive on it

2.4.42-109-M.comment: On the left and right of the road there is a cycle protection lane, which is part of the carriageway and not a cycle lane. This protective lane may also be used by cars, but only if necessary and if cycling traffic is not endangered. As soon as the truck has passed, I have to leave the protective lane again.

2.6.03-117.question_text: You want to connect a trailer with a permissible total mass of over 750 kg to your car. What must you consider?

options.text: The handle of the tow ball coupling must be checked mechanically and visually
The breakaway cable must be properly attached
The lighting equipment of the trailer must be checked for functionality after coupling

2.6.03-117.comment: All three answers are correct. As the driver, you are responsible for ensuring that the trailer is properly and securely attached to the vehicle. You must check the hitch handle, the breakaway cable and the lighting equipment.

2.6.03-118.question_text: You are driving a car with a fully loaded overrun-braked trailer. What special consideration should be taken?

options.text: During longer downhill drives, the trailer brake may overheat
The overrun brake is ineffective when the vehicle combination is standing uphill
Before uncoupling the vehicle combination, the parking brake of the trailer must be applied

2.6.03-118.comment: All three answers are correct. When driving downhill, the trailer pushes on the towing vehicle and the overrun brake brakes. Therefore, when driving downhill for a long time, the trailer brake may overheat. When the vehicle combination is going uphill, the trailer pulls away from the vehicle (downhill). The overrun brake is then ineffective. When uncoupling the trailer from the vehicle, the overrun brake is deactivated. The parking brake must then be applied.

2.6.03-119.question_text: What should be considered when driving a car after you have coupled a caravan?

options.text: the overtaking distance is extended
the acceleration capacity is reduced
the required turning radius when turning is reduced

2.6.03-119.comment: The trailer increases the total weight and the air resistance, which reduces the acceleration capacity and increases the overtaking distance. The greater length leads to a greater space requirement in curves and thus also when turning.

2.6.06-102.question_text: What is referred to as permissible payload?

options.text: The maximum permissible load
The difference between permissible total mass and unladen mass
The permissible total mass

2.6.06-102.comment: The permissible payload - i.e. the maximum permissible load - is not stated in the vehicle registration document. However, it can be determined from two other pieces of information: The difference between the permissible total mass and the unladen mass.

2.7.01-161.question_text: You want to transport furniture with the depicted small van (up to 3.5 t). What must you consider compared to driving a car?

options.text: can tip over more easily in curves
requires special attention to the clearance height
is more susceptible to crosswinds

2.7.01-161.comment: All three answers are correct. The centre of gravity of a van is much higher than that of a car. The larger side area makes it more susceptible to crosswinds. Since vans are often over 2 metres high, special attention must be paid to the clearance height.

2.7.01-162.question_text: How can the Active Parking Assistant assist you when parking?

options.text: detects sufficiently large parking spaces
detects all obstacles while parking
checks whether parking is allowed at a specific location

2.7.01-162.comment: An active parking assistant is a system that is often available as optional equipment in modern vehicles and assists the driver when parking. The system uses sensors and cameras to detect the parking space and measure the dimensions of the vehicle. It then calculates the steering movements required and gives the driver audible and visual instructions on how to turn the steering wheel and operate the accelerator and brake pedals to manoeuvre the vehicle safely into the parking space.

2.7.01-163.question_text: What could be the reason that a turn assist does not reliably detect a cyclist?

options.text: A contamination of the sensor
A concealment of the cyclist by parked vehicles
A damage to the sensor

2.7.01-163.comment: All three answers are correct. Dirt, concealment and damage can cause the turn assist to not function properly.

2.7.01-164.question_text: What must you consider when using the Active Parking Assistant?

options.text: must be manually overridden in case of emerging dangers
exempts me from traffic observation
reliably detects all obstacles while parking

2.7.01-164.comment: The Active Parking Assist uses various sensors to detect whether a parking space is large enough and manoeuvres the vehicle into the space, while the driver only has to operate the accelerator and brake. However, the sensors do not detect all obstacles and do not monitor traffic. I must monitor traffic and the surroundings while using Active Parking Assist and be ready to intervene and override it at any time.

2.7.01-165.question_text: You are driving an electric vehicle. In which case can the braking effect through recuperation be limited?

options.text: with a fully charged battery
below the operating temperature of the battery
in Eco mode

2.7.01-165.comment: The braking effect through recuperation can be limited in an electric vehicle in various situations, e.g: Battery charge level: If the battery of the electric vehicle is already fully charged, the braking effect by recuperation may be limited because the battery cannot absorb any further charge. Low temperatures: At very low temperatures, the performance of the battery may be limited, which may also affect the braking effect by recuperation.

2.7.02-040.question_text: The brake light on your vehicle is not functioning. How should you behave correctly?

options.text: I have the vehicle repaired in a workshop
I try to identify the cause and fix the error myself
I have the brake fluid replaced

2.7.02-040.comment: Defective brake lights impair safe participation in road traffic. Therefore, the lights must be repaired immediately.

2.7.02-138.question_text: You are driving in the dark in an urban area. Oncoming drivers warn you with the high beam. What could this mean in this situation?

options.text: My vehicle dazzles oncoming vehicles
I forgot to turn on the dipped beam
I should turn on the high beam

2.7.02-138.comment: The oncoming traffic seems to be dazzled. This may be caused by incorrectly adjusted headlights. It is also possible that the headlamp levelling control is set incorrectly or has not been adapted to the load condition.

2.7.02-139.question_text: The warning light for the Electronic Stability Control (ESC) in your car is permanently lit. What could this indicate?

options.text: has been deactivated
is defective
is active

2.7.02-139.comment: The Electronic Stability Control (ESC) system is a vehicle safety system designed to improve vehicle stability and control during sudden evasive manoeuvres, poor road conditions or other unexpected situations on the road.
