Only when ESC intervenes (is active) is this indicated by a yellow symbol in the speedometer area. If the yellow ESC symbol is permanently lit, the ESC is deactivated or defective.

2.7.05-006.question_text: What do you need to pay attention to when regularly checking the tires of your vehicle?

options.text: Tire pressure
Tread depth
External damage

2.7.05-006.comment: All three answers are correct. Regularly checking the air pressure is necessary to avoid driving with insufficient pressure. External damage must also be detected at an early stage, otherwise it can lead to a tyre blowout. Regularly checking the tyre tread should ensure that the tyre does not fall below the minimum tread depth.

1.1.06-202-M.question_text: Why are you not allowed to overtake now?

options.text: Because the cyclist might turn left
Because oncoming traffic is being obstructed
Because there is a no overtaking sign

1.1.06-202-M.comment: The cyclist obviously wants to turn left, so I am not allowed to overtake. There are no signs prohibiting overtaking and no oncoming traffic in sight.

options.text: I continue to brake
I stay on my lane for now
I steer to the left now

1.1.07-174-M.comment: The situation is confusing: The truck driver probably wants to drive backwards into the construction site. Due to the proximity of the truck and a car in the blind spot, there is no safe way out. It is necessary to stop and let the truck complete its manoeuvre.

1.1.07-175-M.question_text: What should you expect in this situation?

options.text: The yellow car is turning left
I have to give up my right of way
The pedestrian is crossing the street

1.1.07-175-M.comment: The yellow car approaches quickly and seems to want to turn left immediately. To avoid a dangerous situation, I give up my right of way. The pedestrian continues on the pavement. She is not going to cross the road.

1.2.09-020-M.question_text: Which road user must you give priority to here?

options.text: The pedestrian
The cyclist
The bus

1.2.09-020-M.comment: The pedestrian and the cyclist have priority. The bus is waiting at the traffic lights, it has 'red'.

1.2.34-010.question_text: You are involved in an accident with a vehicle that has the depicted orange sign attached. You see that a liquid is leaking from the vehicle. How should you behave correctly?

options.text: I provide the numbers on the orange sign when making the emergency call
I avoid entering the area with the leaked liquid
I try to seal the leak on the vehicle

1.2.34-010.comment: If a vehicle has an orange warning sign, this means that it is carrying dangerous goods: The vehicle is transporting dangerous goods. This allows the fire and rescue services to prepare for the situation in the event of an accident. Therefore, when making an emergency call, state the numbers on the orange sign and do not enter the area where the liquid has leaked. Under no circumstances should you attempt to plug the leak on the vehicle yourself.

options.text: I must let the yellow car pass
I must let the blue truck pass
I am allowed to drive in front of the yellow car

1.3.01-045-M.comment: At this intersection, priority is given to those coming from the right. This means that you have to drive behind the yellow car. Because you have to turn left, oncoming traffic – in this case the blue truck – has priority.

options.text: I must let the blue car pass
I must stop at the stop line
I must let the red car pass

1.3.01-047-M.comment: The blue car is on the priority road, it is allowed to drive through. I have to stop at the stop line of the STOP sign. Like me, the red car is on a 'give way' road. 'Right before left' applies here, I do not have to let the red car through, but drive in front of the red car.

1.4.40-012.question_text: What danger does this traffic sign warn you about?

options.text: About side winds
About lateral displacement of my vehicle
About air traffic

1.4.40-012.comment: The danger sign 'side wind' can mainly be found in jagged terrain and on bridges. It warns against sideways winds that, depending on their strength, influence the driving behaviour of the vehicle and may require counter-steering. Adjust your speed if necessary.

1.4.41-172.question_text: What applies to this traffic sign?

options.text: It applies between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.
It applies between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m.
It does not apply to electric vehicles

1.4.41-172.comment: The speed limit here is 30 km/h between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.

2.1.04-005.question_text: What do you need to consider in this situation?

options.text: I must drive with special attention
I may be poorly recognizable to other road users
I can estimate distances more easily

2.1.04-005.comment: An avenue is coming up. Due to the constant change of light and shadow, distances and oncoming traffic are often difficult to estimate. At the same time, it makes it more difficult to recognise other motorists, in particular oncoming motorists. If visibility is difficult, the speed must be adjusted.

2.1.04-106.question_text: What increases the risk of accidents?

options.text: when the sun is low in front
with a misted windscreen
with icy side windows

2.1.04-106.comment: Low sun, a misted windscreen and icy side windows impair visibility and therefore mean an increased risk of accidents.

2.1.06-033-M.question_text: Why is overtaking in this situation too dangerous?

options.text: Because vehicles ahead could pull out
Because I cannot see far enough ahead for overtaking
Because there is not enough space to pull back in between the vehicles ahead

2.1.06-033-M.comment: All three answers are correct. Due to the left-hand bend in the road, I cannot see far enough ahead. A vehicle in front could suddenly pull out to overtake and this could lead to a dangerous situation. There is not enough distance between the vehicles ahead. A dangerous situation could arise if I have to pull out again due to oncoming traffic suddenly appearing.

options.text: I brake sharply
I waive my right of way
I continue driving unchanged

2.1.07-025-M.comment: It looks as if the car coming from the left is entering the priority road without paying attention to the right of way and without stopping. To avoid a dangerous situation or even an accident, I brake sharply and waive my right of way.

options.text: I further reduce my speed
I allow the tractor to merge in
I switch to the left lane

2.1.07-026-M.comment: The hard shoulder appears to end just before the tractor, which is why it flashes left to change to the road. The situation is not clearly recognizable, which is precisely why the basic rule of the StVO applies here: § Section 1 (1) Participation in road traffic requires constant caution and mutual consideration. So I reduce my speed and let the tractor pull in. It is not possible to move into the left-hand lane because of oncoming traffic.

options.text: I increase the distance to the vehicle in front
I continue driving with increased attention
I overtake the vehicle in front with a large side distance

2.1.07-028-M.comment: The car in front is driving very erratically and keeps crossing into the oncoming lane. As I don't know the cause and can't assess the further behavior of the car in front, I increase the distance to him and continue driving with increased attention. Overtaking would be too dangerous.

2.1.07-029.question_text: What must you consider when driving on narrow avenues?

options.text: I can often see curves poorly
I must drive particularly defensively
I am protected from icy conditions

2.1.07-029.comment: The many trees are characteristic of avenues. These can impair visibility, especially on bends. The road can be narrow and curved, which requires increased caution and a defensive driving style, especially with oncoming traffic. Avenues do not protect against black ice.

options.text: I reduce my speed
I stay behind the red vehicle for now
I pass the red vehicle quickly

2.1.07-123-M.comment: The car ahead in the right-hand lane is not paying attention or possibly wants to change to the left-hand lane. As I don't know his intention and can't assess his further behavior, I reduce my speed and stay behind him for the time being. Overtaking would be too dangerous.

2.1.08-033-M.question_text: What must you expect when driving on the exit?

options.text: A broken-down vehicle
People on the road
Fallen load

2.1.08-033-M.comment: The curve of the exit is not visible. The warning triangle indicates a possible obstacle on the exit. I must expect a broken-down vehicle, people on the road or a fallen load.

2.1.08-103.question_text: How can you reduce the risk of driving the wrong way on a highway?

options.text: I specifically look for traffic signs for the correct direction at highway entrances
I pay close attention to the signage with changed traffic routing
I only follow the instructions of the navigation system at construction sites

2.1.08-103.comment: One of the main causes of 'wrong-way drivers' are highway entrances and changes in traffic routing. Paying close attention to traffic signs and signage reduces the risk of driving against the prescribed direction. Navigation systems are not up-to-date enough to be a reliable aid, especially at roadworks.

2.1.11-019.question_text: You narrowly avoided a traffic accident due to an emergency brake. Your hands and knees are shaking. How should you behave correctly?

options.text: I take a break as soon as possible to calm down
I will think later about whether I could have avoided the situation
I continue driving immediately to calm down

2.1.11-019.comment: The situation has caused an inner restlessness or even insecurity, which can impair the driver's abilities. An intermediate stop can help you to calm down and continue your journey safely afterwards.

2.2.11-001-M.question_text: Why do you need to be particularly attentive now?

options.text: Because traffic is congested in the street I want to turn into
Because the truck will be very slow when turning
Because the traffic light could change to 'red'

2.2.11-001-M.comment: All three answers are correct. The traffic light can certainly change to 'red' at any time. There is a traffic jam in the street I want to turn into. Therefore, the truck will turn very slowly and probably stop. I must bear in mind that I am not allowed to enter the crossing or junction if I have to wait there despite having right of way or a green light. (§11 StVO)

2.2.14-110.question_text: You want to let a child exit your car. What should you consider?

options.text: - exit on the sidewalk side
- not have to cross the road
- be warned of possible dangers when exiting

2.2.14-110.comment: Anyone getting in or out of the vehicle must behave in such a way that there is no danger to other motorists. This also includes the people who want to get into or out of the vehicle. Increased caution is required, especially for children.

2.2.17-116.question_text: What function should the high beam assistant fulfill in darkness?

options.text: - dims the high beam in good time when there is oncoming traffic
- activates the high beam under suitable environmental conditions
- cleans the headlights for the high beam

2.2.17-116.comment: The high beam assistant analyzes the light conditions and switches the high beam on and off automatically. At the same time, the high beam assistant detects oncoming vehicles and other light sources and automatically switches the high beam off. This means that other road users are no longer dazzled and forgetting to switch on the main beam is reduced. The assistant does not clean the headlights.

2.2.17-117.question_text: In which situation might your vehicle's high beam assistant not dim in time when there is oncoming traffic?

options.text: When crossing a crest
When going through a curve
When dazzled by an oncoming vehicle

2.2.17-117.comment: The high beam assistant detects oncoming vehicles and other light sources and automatically switches off the high beam. On bends and crests, the assistant may detect oncoming traffic too late. In these cases, I have to switch off the high beam myself in good time. If an oncoming vehicle dazzles me, the high beam assistant has certainly recognized this and switched off the high beam.

2.2.18-022.question_text: You want to leave the highway at the next exit. How should you behave in this situation?

options.text: I observe the following traffic
I start to signal right now
I brake evenly to 60 km/h from now on

2.2.18-022.comment: Behavior at Autobahn exits: Move into the right-hand lane in good time and reduce your speed to approx. 100 km/h if necessary. Watch the traffic behind you. Turn right at the 300-meter beacon. Only slow down to approx. 60 km/h on the deceleration lane.

2.2.23-063.question_text: What can cause you to overlook warning signals while driving?

options.text: Listening to loud music
A distraction from talking on the phone
Driving at low engine speed

2.2.23-063.comment: Loud noises, such as a radio that is too loud, can cause warning signals to be ignored. Talking on the phone is also distracting and can cause warning signals to be ignored. Driving at low engine speed does not cause loud noises and therefore does not drown out warning signals.

2.5.01-129.question_text: Your car is equipped with a start-stop system. What advantage does using this vehicle system offer for environmental protection?

options.text: - reduces fuel consumption
- reduces noise pollution
- reduces tire wear

2.5.01-129.comment: The automatic start-stop function is designed to help save fuel. It is particularly useful in city traffic and in traffic jams on Autobahns and country roads. As soon as the car stops - at a red light, for example - the engine is automatically switched off, which also reduces noise pollution. When the car starts up again, the engine is automatically restarted. The system has no influence on tire wear.

2.6.03-120.question_text: You hold a Class B driving license. What trailer are you allowed to tow?

options.text: - up to 750 kg
- over 750 kg, if the total permissible mass of the vehicle combination does not exceed 3,500 kg
- from 3,500 kg

2.6.03-120.comment: In the case of a category B driving licence, the total permissible mass of the car and trailer may not exceed 3,500 kg. In this case, only a trailer with a maximum permissible total mass of 1,100 kg can be considered (3,500 kg - 2,400 kg = 1,100 kg). Accordingly, the trailer with a permissible total mass of 1,000 kg must be selected.

2.7.01-072.question_text: What increases the risk of skidding in curves with poor road conditions?

options.text: Due to a damaged chassis
Due to incorrect tire pressure
Due to incorrect loading

2.7.01-072.comment: A damaged chassis, incorrect tire pressure and incorrect loading increase the risk of skidding when cornering.

2.7.02-044.question_text: How can you recognize a defective turn signal?

options.text: The indicator light for the turn signal flashes faster than usual
By performing a functional test before setting off
The indicator light for the turn signal lights up permanently red

2.7.02-044.comment: If the bulb of a turn signal is defective, this can be recognized by the indicator light flashing faster. Of course, a defective blinker can also be detected by carrying out a functional test before setting off.

2.7.05-107.question_text: This indicator light is on. What could be the cause?

options.text: Too low tire pressure in one tire
A recent wheel change
A loose wheel nut

2.7.05-107.comment: The tire pressure monitoring system constantly monitors the air pressure of the individual tires. If it lights up, the pressure in a tire is too low. It can also light up after a tire change. In this case, the new measured values (if they are correct) must be entered into the system. A loose wheel nut is not recognized by the system.

2.7.06-118-M.question_text: You are using the Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) while driving. The speed is set to 100 km/h. What should you prepare for before the curve?

options.text: The ACC allows my vehicle to accelerate now
I must adjust the speed to the situation
The ACC prompts me to reduce speed

2.7.06-118-M.comment: Adaptive cruise control attempts to follow the vehicle in front in its own lane at a distance set by the driver. If the radar sensor no longer detects a vehicle in front, the speed set by the driver is maintained (again). In this situation, I must expect my vehicle to accelerate because the vehicle in front is no longer detected and I adjust my speed accordingly. The ACC does not prompt me to reduce my speed.

2.7.06-119.question_text: What function does the Emergency Brake Assist serve?

options.text: - warns of the immediate danger of a rear-end collision
- can reduce the risk of injury in an unavoidable collision
- brakes my vehicle when accidentally crossing the lane boundary

2.7.06-119.comment: With Emergency Brake Assist, sensors monitor the surroundings and initially warn the driver of critical situations so that they can react. If the driver brakes, the system increases the brake pressure accordingly and thus helps to reduce the risk of injury. The lane departure warning system is responsible for warning the driver before they cross the lane boundary.

1.1.07-019-M.question_text: You want to turn right at the intersection. What is correct?

options.text: I change lanes as early as possible
I must not obstruct cyclists on the protective lane
I may only cross the protective lane for cyclists at walking speed

1.1.07-019-M.comment: A protective lane for cyclists can be recognised by the fact that it is delimited by a dashed line rather than a solid line. A hard shoulder may also be used by cars, but only if necessary and if it does not obstruct cycle traffic. The speed prescribed for the road applies; walking speed is not required. Changing lanes early is the right thing to do in this situation, also because no other road users are obstructed.

1.1.07-207-M.question_text: How should you behave correctly in this situation?

options.text: I perform an emergency braking maneuver
I continue driving with the brakes ready
I swerve to the right

1.1.07-207-M.comment: The cyclist coming from the left crosses the junction although he should stop. I perform an emergency braking maneuver to avoid an accident.

1.1.10-002.question_text: At which physical signs should you not operate a motor vehicle?

options.text: When feeling nauseous
When feeling dizzy
When having a fever

1.1.10-002.comment: According to the Road Traffic Act, persons who are unable to drive a vehicle safely due to physical defects are prohibited from driving. This applies regardless of whether the physical impairment is temporary or permanent. If you experience nausea, dizziness or fever, you should therefore refrain from driving a motor vehicle.

1.2.03-107.question_text: You are driving on a well-developed road where oncoming traffic can pass you unhindered. Within what distance must you be able to stop in any case?

options.text: - within the distance I can see
- within half the distance I can see
- within double the distance I can see

1.2.03-107.comment: Due to the good road surface and visibility, the following applies: You may only drive as fast as you can stop within the visible distance.

1.2.09-021-M.question_text: You want to leave the roundabout at this exit. What is correct?

options.text: I must let the pedestrian cross the road
I must let the cyclist cross the road
I have priority over the road-crossing road users

1.2.09-021-M.comment: Anyone leaving the roundabout is turning and must therefore give way. The cyclist and the pedestrian have priority, I allow them to cross the road.

1.2.19-009.question_text: The position of the railway barriers has not changed for a long time. How should you behave correctly?

options.text: I do not cross the level crossing
I report the malfunction to the police
I cross the level crossing with special caution

1.2.19-009.comment: Crossing a closed level crossing or, as in this case, a defective level crossing is a dangerous interference with railway operations and poses a considerable risk to life and limb. For this reason, I do not cross the level crossing and report the fault to the police.

1.2.20-109-M.question_text: What must you consider in this situation?

options.text: People could cross the road
I may pass the bus at walking speed
I must not pass the bus

1.2.20-109-M.comment: Passengers could cross the road, which is why increased caution is required. Buses on regular services and marked school buses that stop at bus stops and have their hazard warning lights switched on may only be passed at walking speed and at a distance that excludes any danger to passengers. The walking speed also applies to oncoming traffic on the same carriageway. Passengers must also not be obstructed. If necessary, anyone driving a vehicle must wait.

1.2.37-022-M.question_text: The traffic light has been showing 'green' for your direction for some time. How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: I continue driving with the brakes ready, as the light may change to 'yellow'
I watch the traffic light attentively
I accelerate to safely cross the intersection while it is still 'green'

1.2.37-022-M.comment: The traffic lights have been showing 'green' for some time. I have to expect it to change to amber at any time. So I watch the lights and am ready to brake. As I am travelling at 30 km/h, it would still be possible to stop immediately. Accelerating is out of the question, as there is a speed limit of 30 km/h on the road.

1.4.41-026-M.question_text: What is correct in this situation? I may pass the narrow section

options.text: - after the oncoming car has passed
- before the oncoming car has passed
- only pass at walking speed

1.4.41-026-M.comment: Oncoming traffic must be given priority and may pass through first. Reduce speed and wait if necessary to allow oncoming traffic to pass.

1.4.41-027.question_text: When are you allowed to stop here?

options.text: On Sundays
On public holidays
On Saturdays

1.4.41-027.comment: 'Working days' refers to the days from Monday to Saturday. Sundays, public holidays and public holidays are not working days.

2.1.03-044-M.question_text: What must you expect in this situation?

options.text: My motor vehicle may be pushed to the left
When entering the slipstream of the truck, my motor vehicle may be pushed to the right
The truck in front may be pushed to the right

2.1.03-044-M.comment: The wind vane signals a strong crosswind from the right, so your vehicle will be forced leftwards. When entering the slipstream of the lorry, the crosswind is no longer as strong, causing your own car to pull to the right. The lorry in front is pushed to the left, but not to the right.

2.1.05-010.question_text: What should you expect when driving on the motorway at very high speed?

options.text: Other road users underestimate my speed
Crosswinds may affect my driving stability
I may not be able to react to dangers in time

2.1.05-010.comment: Due to the fast approach, there is a risk of being recognised too late by other road users. The higher the speed, the greater the impact of crosswinds on driving stability. The reaction distance increases considerably with increasing speed. At 200 km/h, it takes around 60 metres to recognise the danger and react.

2.1.06-035-M.question_text: The vehicles in front of you are driving at about 30 km/h. Why are you not allowed to overtake before the curve?

options.text: Because my overtaking distance is too long
Because the red car could pull out to overtake
Because I must not cross the guideline

2.1.06-035-M.comment: The overtaking distance to the bend is short, which makes overtaking too dangerous. Also because there could be oncoming traffic at any time. In addition, the red car could pull out to overtake. I could cross the dashed line.

2.1.06-107-M.question_text: Why should you not overtake the moped rider in this situation?

options.text: Because the moped rider could fall
Because I must not drive significantly faster than the moped rider
Because I cannot maintain the required side distance

2.1.06-107-M.comment: In the roadworks area, the carriageway is narrowed and the maximum permitted speed is limited to 30 km/h by traffic signs. I do not overtake because I cannot maintain the required amount of side clearance and I cannot overtake the moped rider travelling at approx. 25 km/h much faster. There is an increased risk of the moped rider falling due to the dirty carriageway.

2.1.11-020.question_text: While driving, you are very annoyed by the behavior of another road user. How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: I continue to concentrate on the traffic
I drive in such a way that my anger does not negatively affect traffic safety
I take a break if necessary to calm down

2.1.11-020.comment: All three answers are correct. I continue driving in a concentrated manner and make sure that my anger does not negatively affect my ability to drive. If this is not possible, I take a break and only continue driving when I have calmed down.

options.text: I stay behind the tractor
I expect the tractor to turn
I follow the overtaking signal given by the tractor driver through blinking

2.2.05-021-M.comment: The rest of the road is difficult to see and obscured by the tractor, so I don't overtake. The tractor also seems to want to turn right and has not asked me to overtake.

options.text: I switch to the right lane
I stay in the middle lane
I switch to the left lane

2.2.07-004.comment: In principle, the right-hand lane rule must be observed on multi- or three-lane roads. One exception to this rule is if - even occasionally - a vehicle is travelling slightly slower than me in the right-hand lane. There is no slow-moving vehicle in sight in the right-hand lane. I therefore move over to the right-hand lane.

2.2.09-010-M.question_text: You want to turn left. Which driving line must you follow?

options.text: The middle driving line
The left driving line
The right driving line

2.2.09-010-M.comment: You are on a one-way street where there may be oncoming traffic from cyclists. I must not endanger potential cyclists and, according to StVO §9, I must keep as far to the left as possible when turning left. I therefore ride in the centre lane.

2.2.09-011-M.question_text: You want to turn left. Which driving line must you follow?

options.text: The left driving line
The middle driving line
The right driving line

2.2.09-011-M.comment: If you want to turn left, you must keep your vehicle as far to the left as possible. As this is a one-way street and there is therefore no oncoming traffic, you should choose the leftmost driving line.

2.2.17-118.question_text: Your car's automatic lighting system is activated. What must you expect under the given lighting conditions?

options.text: The low beam does not turn on automatically
I will be seen late by following road users
The automatic lighting system turns on the fog lights

2.2.17-118.comment: In cloudy visibility conditions, as shown in the picture, the sensors of the automatic lighting system often do not react sensitively enough and the low beam is not activated automatically. The activated daytime running lights also only cover the front of the vehicle. The rear lights remain unlit, which is why I am only seen late by following road users. The automatic light system does not switch on the fog lights in poor visibility.

options.text: I reduce my speed
I accelerate
I switch to the middle lane

2.2.18-023-M.comment: The blue vehicle is in the merging lane and is accelerating. I have to allow it to merge. I therefore reduce my speed. A vehicle is travelling next to me in the middle lane. Therefore, I do not change to the centre lane.

2.2.23-125.question_text: While driving, the front windshield of your vehicle fogs up from the inside. How can you counteract this?

options.text: I turn on the air conditioning
I direct the ventilation at maximum power to the windshield
I open the windows when the outside air humidity is high

2.2.23-125.comment: Misted-up windows occur when humidity condenses on the car windows. To clear the view again, you should not open the windows when the outdoor humidity level is high. The quickest way to do this is to switch on the air conditioning and direct the ventilation towards the windscreen at maximum power.

2.2.36-001-M.question_text: How do you behave when approaching this heavy transport correctly?

options.text: I switch to the right lane
I do not overtake
I overtake with great caution

2.2.36-001-M.comment: There is a mobile traffic sign "No overtaking" on the heavy goods transport escort vehicle, which has the same meaning as a stationary traffic sign. I am not overtaking. I change to the right-hand lane due to the right-hand driving ban.

2.4.42-008-M.question_text: What applies after this traffic sign?

options.text: - I may choose the lane freely for my direction
- I may drive faster in the right lane than vehicles in the left lane
- I may drive faster than 50 km/h due to the multi-lane road

2.4.42-008-M.comment: The direction sign "Ortstafel Vorderseite" indicates the beginning of a built-up area. The maximum permitted speed is 50 km/h. Vehicles with a maximum permissible mass of up to 3.5 tonnes have a free choice of lanes.

2.7.01-166.question_text: Your vehicle is equipped with a hill start assist. What advantage does this assistance system offer you?

options.text: - it prevents my vehicle from rolling back unintentionally
- it takes over the release of the brake
- it drives all wheels simultaneously

2.7.01-166.comment: The hill start assist system provides automated support when starting off on slopes. It prevents the vehicle from rolling backwards and releases the brakes when starting off. It has no influence on the simultaneous drive of the wheels.

2.7.02-049.question_text: A display in your liquid-cooled vehicle informs you of an excessively high engine temperature. How should you behave now?

options.text: I stop as quickly as possible at a suitable place
I continue driving slowly with increased engine speed for better engine cooling
I continue driving in a low gear until the next planned stop

2.7.02-049.comment: If the engine temperature is too high, stop at a suitable place as quickly as possible to avoid possible engine damage. Continuing to drive, especially with increased engine speed, has the opposite effect, the engine temperature continues to rise.

2.7.02-050.question_text: A display in your liquid-cooled vehicle informs you of an excessively high coolant temperature. What could be the cause?

options.text: The radiator is contaminated
The radiator fan has failed
The cooling system is leaking

2.7.02-050.comment: Cooling performance is impaired if the radiator is contaminated or the cooling fan fails. A leaking cooling system leads to a loss of coolant, which also reduces the cooling capacity. All three reasons can lead to an excessively high coolant temperature.

2.8.01-014.question_text: A driving license applicant practices driving without an instructor in public traffic. What should he expect if he is controlled by the police?

options.text: With a criminal proceeding
With a check of fitness to drive
With no consequences if a license holder is in the vehicle

2.8.01-014.comment: Driving without a licence can have serious legal consequences. If you are caught driving without a licence, you may be subject to a fitness to drive check. This can also result in criminal proceedings.

1.1.07-176-M.question_text: How should you behave correctly now?

options.text: I brake
I swerve to the left
I continue driving steadily

1.1.07-176-M.comment: The cyclist on the pavement is very likely to avoid the obstacle on the pavement and ride onto the road. I cannot swerve to the left because of the vehicle on my left and continuing to drive steadily would lead to a dangerous situation with the cyclist. So I brake.

1.2.09-022-M.question_text: You want to turn right here. What is correct?

options.text: I must let both pedestrians cross the road
I must let only the oncoming pedestrian cross the road
I have priority over both pedestrians

1.2.09-022-M.comment: If you want to turn, you must let oncoming vehicles pass, rail vehicles, bicycles with auxiliary motors and cyclists even if they are travelling on or next to the carriageway in the same direction. Special consideration must be given to pedestrians. Wait if necessary.

1.2.10-006-M.question_text: You want to exit the gas station. What is correct?

options.text: I must give way to crossing pedestrians
I may exit in both directions
I have priority over vehicles coming from the left

1.2.10-006-M.comment: When entering a road from a property or car park, there must be no danger to other road users. I must give way to other vehicles. I have to drive over a pavement; pedestrians crossing the road always have priority. The blue traffic sign with the white arrow means "prescribed direction of travel right", so I may only turn right.

1.2.19-117.question_text: You want to cross a level crossing with open barriers. What is correct?

options.text: I must approach the level crossing at a moderate speed
I expect bumps when crossing the level crossing
I may only cross the tracks at walking speed

1.2.19-117.comment: Road traffic may only approach such level crossings at a moderate speed. There are always bumps in the road at level crossings caused by the rails running across. However, walking speed is not usually necessary or prescribed. If the level crossing cannot be crossed quickly and without stopping due to road traffic, you must wait in front of the St Andrew's cross.

options.text: - stop in front of the St Andrew's cross
- cross the level crossing quickly
- continue driving with the barrier open

1.2.19-118-M.comment: Yellow means: "Wait for the next signal before the crossing". If I can stop in front of the traffic lights with medium braking and without endangering others behind me, I must stop in front of the St Andrew's cross.

1.2.20-110-M.question_text: What is correct in this situation?

options.text: I may pass the bus at most at walking speed
The blue car must stop
I may continue driving at unchanged speed

1.2.20-110-M.comment: You are allowed to pass buses on regular routes and marked school buses that stop at bus stops and have their hazard warning lights switched on at walking speed.

1.2.20-111-M.question_text: What must you consider in this situation?

options.text: People could cross the roadway
I may only pass the stationary bus at walking speed
I may not pass the stationary bus

1.2.20-111-M.comment: You may pass buses on regular services and marked school buses that stop at bus stops and have their hazard warning lights switched on at walking speed. People could still quickly cross the carriageway to reach the bus.

1.2.36-016-M.question_text: What is correct in this situation?

options.text: I must wait before the junction
I may turn right without waiting
I must turn around

1.2.36-016-M.comment: When a police officer directing traffic stretches out one or both arms across the direction of travel, this means: "Stop before the junction". This means I have to wait in front of the junction and am not allowed to turn right. I am also not allowed to turn round, because otherwise I would cross the solid white line.

options.text: I start now
I only start when the truck moves on
I only start when my traffic light shows 'green'

1.2.37-104.comment: At a two-phase traffic light that does not have a green signal, I may continue driving if no signal lights up. The fact that the lorry stops at the next set of traffic lights is no reason to wait, as I can stop behind the lorry without blocking the junction.

options.text: I let the tram pass
I let the tractor turn
I go first

1.3.01-051-M.comment: As a left-turner, it is necessary to give priority to the approaching tram. I let the tram through. I have priority over the tractor.

options.text: I may cross the intersection
I may turn right
I may turn left

1.4.41-028-M.comment: The red and white triangle (sign 205) means that I must give way at the junction. I may cross the junction if (as here) there is no vehicle on the road with right of way. Turning left or right is not prescribed here.

1.4.41-029.question_text: What does this traffic sign indicate?

options.text: Vehicles of all kinds are not allowed to drive on this road
Vehicles of all kinds may drive at walking speed
Vehicles of all kinds may drive as residents

1.4.41-029.comment: The traffic sign indicates that vehicles of any kind are prohibited from travelling on this road. The sign does not apply to manual vehicles, riders, drivers of horses, drivers and drivers of livestock. Motorbikes and bicycles may be pushed.

1.4.41-030.question_text: You are driving on a one-way street marked this way. What is correct?

options.text: I must position myself as far left as possible to turn left
I may also park at the left edge of the roadway
I may park against the direction of traffic

1.4.41-030.comment: In one-way streets, I have to get as far to the left as possible in order to turn left. Parking is permitted on the left-hand side of the road. Parking against the direction of traffic is not permitted.

1.4.41-173.question_text: How must you behave with this traffic sign?

options.text: I must signal left
I must turn left before the traffic sign
I must turn left after the traffic sign

1.4.41-173.comment: Anyone driving a vehicle must follow the prescribed direction of travel. At traffic sign 211-10 "Prescribed direction of travel here left", I must turn left before the traffic sign. If you want to turn off, you must announce this clearly and in good time, using the direction indicators.

1.5.01-017.question_text: In which situation should you turn off the engine to save fuel and reduce environmental impact?

options.text: If I have to wait in traffic for a foreseeable longer time
If I have to wait at a level crossing
If I have to stop at a 'Stop' sign

1.5.01-017.comment: Switching off the engine helps the environment if there is a foreseeable longer wait, such as at railway crossings or during traffic jams. This saves fuel and reduces pollution. Short stops, such as at stop signs, do not require the engine to be switched off.

options.text: I reduce my speed
I drive as far to the right as possible
I signal to the motorcyclist that he can overtake me

2.1.07-124-M.comment: The road is relatively narrow and a lorry is coming towards me. I therefore drive as far to the right as possible and reduce my speed. The motorcyclist should not overtake in this situation, so I do not signal to him to overtake.

options.text: I reduce my speed
I let the blue car in front of me merge
I accelerate

2.2.07-014-M.comment: To avoid a dangerous situation, I reduce my speed and let the car in front of me move over. As the speed limit is 80 km/h, I cannot accelerate.

2.2.18-024-M.question_text: What do you have to expect now?

options.text: - to brake
- to stay in the middle lane
- to accelerate

2.2.18-024-M.comment: There seems to be an end of a traffic jam on the bend. The braking vehicles and the hazard warning lights switched on are a sure sign of this. The lorry in front of me will slow down and stay in the middle lane as there are vehicles to its left and right. It will certainly not accelerate.

2.2.23-126.question_text: Your vehicle is covered in snow. How must you behave before starting your journey?

options.text: - remove it from the license plate
- remove it from the vehicle roof
- remove it from the lighting equipment

2.2.23-126.comment: Snow and ice must be completely removed from the licence plate. If the licence plate is not legible, you will be fined. Snow and ice must also be removed from the roof so that no parts can come loose while driving and endanger other road users. It goes without saying that all lighting equipment must be free of snow.

2.2.23-127.question_text: Which parts of your vehicle must you completely free from snow and ice before starting your journey?

options.text: The windscreen
The exterior mirrors
The side windows

2.2.23-127.comment: Snow and ice must be completely removed from the windscreen and mirrors to ensure the best possible visibility. The same applies to headlights and lights.

2.2.23-128.question_text: You want to start a journey in winter weather conditions. What must you consider?

options.text: - can cause accidents
- can damage other vehicles
- can impair your own visibility forward

2.2.23-128.comment: Snow and ice must be removed from the roof so that parts of it do not come loose while driving and endanger other road users.

options.text: I accelerate
I maintain my speed
I only accelerate when the speed limit is lifted by a traffic sign

2.4.41-005-M.comment: A speed limit ends after a roadworks, even if there is no sign indicating the end of the roadworks. However, I must be sure that the roadworks have really ended.

2.4.42-110.question_text: Which document allows you to park here?

options.text: My EU parking permit for severely disabled persons
The EU parking permit of a severely disabled person I am transporting
My resident parking permit

2.4.42-110.comment: Parking here is only permitted for people with a special EU parking card. The disability card alone is not sufficient.

2.5.01-130.question_text: You are driving a car with a plug-in hybrid drive. How can you optimize fuel consumption?

options.text: I regularly charge the battery from the power grid
I use the electric drive through my driving style
I only use recuperation to charge the battery

2.5.01-130.comment: I regularly charge the battery using the mains supply so that I can drive electrically as often as possible. Due to my driving style, e.g. no high speeds on the motorway or no heavy acceleration and braking, the electric drive is used more often.

2.6.03-121.question_text: What can impair the driving stability of a towed trailer?

options.text: A load center of gravity located far back in the trailer
A too low tire pressure of the trailer tires
A leaking shock absorber

2.6.03-121.comment: For good driving stability, the load should be distributed so that the centre of gravity is as far as possible above the axle of the trailer and heavy loads are placed in the area of the axle(s). Insufficient tyre pressure and leaking shock absorbers also impair the driving stability of the trailer.

2.6.06-104.question_text: What applies when operating vehicles regarding vehicle height including the height of the load?

options.text: I must inform myself about the vehicle height in the registration certificate part I
I must determine the actual height for loads extending beyond the vehicle outline
I must comply with the legally permissible height of a maximum of 4.5 m

2.6.06-104.comment: You must observe the prohibitions on actual height and are obliged to inform yourself about the actual dimensions of the vehicle including load.

2.7.01-167.question_text: What applies when using driver assistance systems for the longitudinal and lateral control of your motor vehicle?

options.text: I must know the system limits of the driver assistance system
I must immediately override the driver assistance system in case of a malfunction
I can leave the longitudinal and lateral control to the driver assistance system when tired

2.7.01-167.comment: Driver assistance systems can raise false expectations, causing drivers to overestimate the possibilities of the technology. There is a risk that drivers place too much trust in the systems and therefore do not follow the traffic situation sufficiently. I must therefore always be able to override the driver assistance system immediately in the event of a malfunction.

2.7.02-140.question_text: The seat belt for the front passenger in your car is defective. How should you behave correctly?

options.text: I will have the seat belt repaired
I will not allow any passenger to ride along
I will adjust the seat belt height adjustment

2.7.02-140.comment: The facts are clear: StVO §21a Seat belts, ...(1) Mandatory seat belts must be worn while driving; ... Therefore, the seat may no longer be used and the seat belt must be replaced.

1.4.40-013.question_text: You are driving on a road with one lane for each direction. At which traffic sign must you generally give way to oncoming traffic?
1.4.40-013.comment: Correct: 121 - Lane narrowed on one side There is a clear narrowing of the carriageway on the right-hand lane. I must give priority to oncoming traffic. 208 - Priority for oncoming traffic Incorrect: 125 - Oncoming traffic

1.4.41-031.question_text: You are driving on a priority road. Which traffic sign ends your priority?
1.4.41-031.comment: Correct 205 - Give way 307 - End of the priority road Wrong 301 - Give way The sign indicates that you have right of way at the next junction or intersection.

1.4.41-032.question_text: At which traffic regulation must you generally stop before turning right?
1.4.41-032.comment: Right 206 - Stop. Give way. Anyone driving a vehicle must stop and give way. 720 - Green arrow You must stop before turning. Wrong 301 - Give way

1.4.41-033.question_text: Which traffic sign prohibits you from entering the designated area?
1.4.41-033.comment: Correct 242.1 - Beginning of a pedestrian zone No traffic other than pedestrians may use the pedestrian zone. 267 - Prohibition of entry Incorrect 208 - Priority of oncoming traffic

1.4.41-174.question_text: At which traffic sign is turning prohibited?
1.4.41-174.comment: Correct 272 - Prohibition of turning 330.1 - Start of a motorway Turning is prohibited on the motorway. 327 - Tunnel Turning is prohibited in a tunnel.

1.4.41-175.question_text: From which traffic sign must you not exceed a permissible maximum speed of 60 km/h?
1.4.41-175.comment: Correct 274: Permitted maximum speed Anyone driving a vehicle must not drive faster than the maximum speed indicated. Incorrect 278: End of the maximum authorised speed 275: Prescribed minimum speed

1.4.42-011.question_text: From which traffic sign may you only proceed at walking speed?
1.4.42-011.comment: Correct 325.1 - Beginning of a traffic-calmed area The following rule applies in this area: "Anyone driving a vehicle must drive at walking speed." Incorrect No walking speed is prescribed for the other signs.

1.4.42-012.question_text: At which traffic sign do you generally have the right of way at the next intersection?
1.4.42-012.comment: Right of way - The sign indicates that you have right of way at the next junction or intersection. Incorrect - Intersection or junction with right of way from the right - Priority over oncoming traffic

1.2.34-011.question_text: Which emergency number can you call to reach the emergency medical services throughout Europe?
1.2.34-011.comment: You can call the emergency control centre free of charge anywhere in Europe on 112. This connects you directly to the emergency medical services, police and fire brigade.

2.2.03-026-M.question_text: What is the maximum speed you are allowed to drive at after turning?
2.2.03-026-M.comment: Unless otherwise indicated, the maximum speed in built-up areas is 50 km/h. The 30 km/h limit on the previous priority road no longer applies here.

2.2.03-109.question_text: You are driving a vehicle combination consisting of a motor vehicle with a maximum permissible mass of up to 3,5 t and a trailer without approval for 100 km/h. What is the maximum speed you are allowed to drive at on motorways?
2.2.03-109.comment: The maximum speed for vehicle combinations with a maximum permissible mass of up to 3,5 t and a trailer is 80 km/h outside built-up areas.

2.2.03-110.question_text: You are driving a vehicle combination consisting of a motor vehicle with a maximum permissible mass of up to 3,5 t and a trailer approved for 100 km/h. What is the maximum speed you are allowed to drive at on a federal road that is not a road reserved for motor vehicles?
2.2.03-110.comment: The maximum permitted speed on federal roads is 80 km/h. You may drive at 100 km/h only on motorways and designated roads reserved for motor vehicles, provided your trailer has the necessary approval.

2.6.06-103.question_text: What is the maximum permitted length of a vehicle combination consisting of a passenger car and a trailer, without a projecting load?
2.6.06-103.comment: Without a load, your passenger car and trailer may be up to 18,00 m long.

2.7.05-108.question_text: What is the legally required minimum depth of the main tread on all tyres of your passenger car?
2.7.05-108.comment: The legally required minimum tyre tread depth is 1,6 mm. The main tread consists of the grooves in the central areas of the tread surface.
